bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起強圉大荒落，盡玄黓閹茂，凡六年。

translations.literal: From Qiangyu Dahuangluo through Xuanyi Yanmao; six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Qiangyu Dahuangluo through Xuanyi Yanmao—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十一月，乙丑，薛澤免。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, on yichou, Xue Ze was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, on yichou, Xue Ze was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以公孫弘為丞相，封平津侯。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingjin.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingjin.

sentences.zh: 丞相封侯自弘始。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment of a chancellor as marquis began with Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment of a chancellor as marquis began with Hong.

sentences.zh: 時上方興功業，弘於是開東閤以延賢人，與參謀議。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was just then raising great undertakings; Hong thereupon opened the eastern gate to receive worthy men and deliberate with them in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then raising great undertakings; Hong opened the eastern gate to receive worthy men and take counsel with them.

sentences.zh: 每朝覲奏事，因言國家便宜，上亦使左右文學之臣與之論難。

translations.literal: At each court audience when he reported on affairs, he would thereby speak of what was expedient for the state; the emperor also had literary scholars at his side debate with him.
translations.idiomatic: At each audience, as he reported on affairs, he would speak of what served the state; the emperor also set literary scholars at his side to debate him.

sentences.zh: 弘嘗奏言：「十賊彍弩，百吏不敢前。

translations.literal: Hong once memorialized, saying: "Ten thieves drawing crossbows—a hundred officials dare not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hong once memorialized, saying, "Ten thieves with drawn crossbows, and a hundred officials dare not advance.

sentences.zh: 請禁民毋得挾弓弩，便。

translations.literal: I request that the people be forbidden to carry bow and crossbow—it would be expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Forbid the people to carry bow and crossbow—that would be expedient.

sentences.zh: 」上下其議。

translations.literal: " The memorial was passed up and down for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was circulated for discussion.

sentences.zh: 侍中吾丘壽王對曰：「臣聞古者作五兵，非以相害，以禁暴討邪也。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wuqiu Shouwang replied: "Your servant has heard that in antiquity the five weapons were made not to harm one another but to restrain violence and punish wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wuqiu Shouwang replied, "I have heard that in antiquity the five weapons were made not to harm one another but to restrain violence and punish wickedness.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，銷甲兵，折鋒刃；

translations.literal: Qin united all under Heaven, melted armor and weapons, and broke sharp blades;
translations.idiomatic: Qin united the realm, melted armor and weapons, and broke every sharp blade;

sentences.zh: 其後民以耰鋤、棰梃相撻擊，犯法滋眾，盜賊不勝，卒以亂亡。

translations.literal: afterward the people used hoes and clubs to strike one another; lawbreakers grew ever more numerous, bandits could not be overcome, and in the end they perished in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: afterward the people took up hoes and clubs to strike one another; lawbreakers multiplied, bandits could not be checked, and the dynasty perished in disorder.

sentences.zh: 故聖王務教化而省禁防，知其不足恃也。

translations.literal: Hence the sage kings devoted themselves to transforming through teaching and reduced prohibitions and guards, knowing that these were not sufficient to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Hence sage kings devoted themselves to teaching and reduced prohibitions and guards, knowing they could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：『男子生，桑弧、蓬矢以舉之，』明示有事也。

translations.literal: The Rites say: 'When a boy is born, a mulberry bow and rush arrows are raised for him'—openly showing that there are affairs to attend to.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, 'When a boy is born, a mulberry bow and rush arrows are raised for him'—openly showing that life holds duties to perform.

sentences.zh: 大射之禮，自天子降及庶人，三代之道也。

translations.literal: The rites of the great archery contest, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, were the Way of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of the great archery contest, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, were the Way of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 愚聞聖王合射以明教矣，未聞弓矢之為禁也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that sage kings joined archery to make teaching clear; he has not heard of bow and arrow as a prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that sage kings joined archery to make teaching clear; I have never heard of bow and arrow as a prohibition.

sentences.zh: 且所為禁者，為盜賊之以攻奪也；

translations.literal: Moreover, what is to be prohibited is what bandits use for attack and seizure;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what should be prohibited is what bandits use for attack and seizure;

sentences.zh: 攻奪之罪死，然而不止者，大奸之於重誅，固不避也。

translations.literal: the crime of attack and seizure is death, yet those who do not cease are great villains toward heavy punishment—they certainly do not avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: attack and seizure are capital crimes, yet those who do not cease are great villains—they do not shrink from heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣恐邪人挾之而吏不能止，良民以自備而抵法禁，是擅賊威而奪民救也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that wicked men will carry them while officers cannot stop them, and good people will ready themselves for self-defense yet run against the law—this is to monopolize the bandits' power and seize the people's means of rescue.
translations.idiomatic: I fear wicked men will carry them while officers cannot stop them, and good people who arm themselves for defense will run afoul of the law—this is to hand bandits power and strip the people of their means of rescue.

sentences.zh: 竊以為大不便。

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks it greatly inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe it would be greatly inexpedient.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上以難弘，弘詘服焉。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor used it to press Hong, and Hong was defeated and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor used it to press Hong, and Hong was defeated and yielded.

sentences.zh: 弘性意忌，外寬內深。

translations.literal: Hong by nature was suspicious and jealous, outwardly lenient but inwardly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was by nature suspicious and jealous, outwardly lenient but inwardly deep.

sentences.zh: 諸嘗與弘有隙，無近遠，雖陽與善，後竟報其過。

translations.literal: All who had once had a rift with Hong, near or far, though he outwardly treated them well, in the end he still repaid their faults.
translations.idiomatic: All who had once crossed him, near or far, though he treated them kindly to their faces, in the end he repaid every fault.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒為人廉直，以弘為從諛，弘嫉之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu was by nature upright and incorruptible; he regarded Hong as a flatterer, and Hong resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu was upright and incorruptible; he regarded Hong as a flatterer, and Hong resented him.

sentences.zh: 膠西王端驕恣，數犯法，所殺傷二千石甚眾。

translations.literal: King Duan of Jiaoxi was arrogant and willful, repeatedly violated the law, and killed or wounded very many officials at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: King Duan of Jiaoxi was arrogant and willful, repeatedly broke the law, and killed or wounded a great many senior officials.

sentences.zh: 弘乃薦仲舒為膠西相；

translations.literal: Hong then recommended Zhongshu as Chancellor of Jiaoxi;
translations.idiomatic: Hong then recommended Zhongshu as Chancellor of Jiaoxi;

sentences.zh: 仲舒以病免。

translations.literal: Zhongshu resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 汲黯常毀儒，面觸弘，弘欲誅之以事，乃言上曰：「右內史界部中多貴臣、宗室，難治，非素重臣不能任，請徙黯為右內史。

translations.literal: Ji An often disparaged the Ru and confronted Hong to his face; Hong wished to destroy him through an affair and therefore told the emperor: "Within the Right Metropolitan Steward's jurisdiction there are many noble ministers and members of the imperial clan; it is hard to govern and only a minister of longstanding weight can bear the post—I request that Ji An be transferred to Right Metropolitan Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An often disparaged the Ru and confronted Hong to his face; Hong wished to destroy him by other means and told the emperor, "The Right Metropolitan Steward's jurisdiction holds many noble ministers and members of the imperial clan; it is hard to govern, and only a minister of longstanding weight can bear the post—I request that Ji An be transferred to Right Metropolitan Steward.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, there was a great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: ----3匈奴右賢王數侵擾朔方。

translations.literal: ----3 The Xiongnu Right Worthy King repeatedly harassed Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Xiongnu Right Worthy King repeatedly harassed Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 天子令車騎將軍青將三萬騎出高闕，衛尉蘇建為游擊將軍，左內史李沮為強弩將軍，太僕公孫賀為騎將軍，代相李蔡為輕車將軍，皆領屬車騎將軍，俱出朔方；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered Chariots and Cavalry General Qing to lead thirty thousand horsemen out through Gaoque Pass; Commandant of the Guard Su Jian was made Mobile Strike General, Left Metropolitan Steward Li Ju was made Powerful Crossbow General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He was made Cavalry General, Chancellor of Dai Li Cai was made Light Chariot General—all were placed under the Chariots and Cavalry General and marched out together from Shuofang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chariots and Cavalry General Qing to lead thirty thousand horsemen out through Gaoque Pass; Commandant of the Guard Su Jian was made Mobile Strike General, Left Metropolitan Steward Li Ju Powerful Crossbow General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He Cavalry General, and Chancellor of Dai Li Cai Light Chariot General—all under the Chariots and Cavalry General, marching together from Shuofang;

sentences.zh: 大行李息、岸頭侯張次公為將軍，俱出右北平；

translations.literal: Grand Herald Li Xi and Marquis of Antou Zhang Cigong were made generals and marched out together from Right Beiping;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Herald Li Xi and Marquis of Antou Zhang Cigong were made generals and marched out together from Right Beiping;

sentences.zh: 凡十餘萬人，擊匈奴。

translations.literal: more than a hundred thousand men in all struck the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand men in all struck the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 右賢王以為漢兵遠，不能至，飲酒，醉。

translations.literal: The Right Worthy King thought the Han troops were far away and could not arrive; he drank wine and became drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Worthy King thought the Han troops were far away and could not reach him; he drank himself drunk.

sentences.zh: 衛青等兵出塞六七百里，夜至，圍右賢王。

translations.literal: Wei Qing and the others' troops went out of the pass six or seven hundred li, arrived by night, and surrounded the Right Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing and the others marched six or seven hundred li beyond the pass, arrived by night, and surrounded the Right Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 右賢王驚，夜逃，獨與壯騎數百馳，潰圍北去。

translations.literal: The Right Worthy King was alarmed, fled by night, and with only several hundred stalwart horsemen galloped alone, breaking the encirclement and fleeing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Worthy King was alarmed, fled by night, and with only several hundred stalwart horsemen galloped north alone, breaking through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 得右賢裨王十餘人，眾男女萬五千餘人，畜數十百萬，於是引兵而還。

translations.literal: They took more than ten of the Right Worthy King's subordinate kings, a multitude of men and women of more than fifteen thousand, and livestock numbering in the millions of tens; thereupon they led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than ten of the Right Worthy King's subordinate kings, more than fifteen thousand men and women, and livestock numbering in the tens of millions; thereupon they led the army back.

sentences.zh: 至塞，天子使使者持大將軍印，即軍中拜衛青為大將軍，諸將皆屬焉。

translations.literal: When they reached the pass, the Son of Heaven sent an envoy bearing the Grand General's seal and, right in the army, invested Wei Qing as Grand General; all the generals were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: At the pass the emperor sent an envoy bearing the Grand General's seal and, right in camp, invested Wei Qing as Grand General; all the generals were placed under him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，復益封青八千七百戶，封青三子伉、不疑、登皆為列侯。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Qing's fief was again increased by eight thousand seven hundred households, and Qing's three sons Kang, Buyi, and Deng were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Qing's fief was again increased by eight thousand seven hundred households, and his three sons Kang, Buyi, and Deng were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 青固謝曰：「臣幸得待罪行間，賴陛下神靈，軍大捷，皆諸校尉力戰之功也。

translations.literal: Qing firmly declined, saying: "Your servant has been fortunate to attend in the ranks of those who bear punishment; relying on Your Majesty's numinous power, the army won a great victory—all of it is the merit of the colonels' fierce fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Qing firmly declined, saying, "I have been fortunate to serve in the ranks of those who bear punishment; relying on Your Majesty's numinous power, the army won a great victory—all of it is the merit of the colonels' fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 陛下幸已益封臣青；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already been pleased to increase your servant Qing's fief;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already been pleased to increase my fief;

sentences.zh: 臣青子在襁褓中，未有勤勞，上列地封為三侯，非臣待罪行間所以勸士力戰之意也。

translations.literal: your servant Qing's sons are still in swaddling clothes and have no merit of toil; to rank them with territories and enfeoff them as three marquises is not what your servant, attending in the ranks of those who bear punishment, means by encouraging officers to fight fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: my sons are still in swaddling clothes and have done no labor; to rank them with territories and enfeoff them as three marquises is not what I mean by encouraging officers to fight fiercely.

sentences.zh: 」天子曰：「我非忘諸校尉功也。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven said: "I have not forgotten the colonels' merit.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I have not forgotten the colonels' merit.

sentences.zh: 」乃封護軍都尉公孫敖為合騎侯，都尉韓說為龍額侯，公孫賀為南窌侯，李蔡為樂安侯，校尉李朔為涉軹侯，趙不虞為隨成侯，公孫戎奴為從平侯，李沮、李息及校尉豆如意皆賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Protector-General of the Army Colonel Gongsun Ao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Heqi, Colonel Han Shuo as Marquis of Long'e, Gongsun He as Marquis of Nanjiao, Li Cai as Marquis of Le'an, Colonel Li Shuo as Marquis of Shezhi, Zhao Buyu as Marquis of Suicheng, Gongsun Rongnu as Marquis of Congping, and Li Ju, Li Xi, and Colonel Dou Ruyi were all granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Protector-General of the Army Colonel Gongsun Ao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Heqi, Colonel Han Shuo as Marquis of Long'e, Gongsun He as Marquis of Nanjiao, Li Cai as Marquis of Le'an, Colonel Li Shuo as Marquis of Shezhi, Zhao Buyu as Marquis of Suicheng, Gongsun Rongnu as Marquis of Congping, and Li Ju, Li Xi, and Colonel Dou Ruyi were all granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 於是青尊寵，於群臣無二，公卿以下皆卑奉之，獨汲黯與亢禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qing's honor and favor were without peer among the ministers; from high ministers down all served him humbly—only Ji An matched him in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Qing's honor and favor had no peer among the ministers; from high ministers down all served him humbly—only Ji An matched him in ceremony.

sentences.zh: 人或說黯曰：「自天子欲群臣下大將軍，大將軍尊重，君不可以不拜。

translations.literal: Someone urged Ji An, saying: "Since the Son of Heaven wishes the ministers to rank below the Grand General, and the Grand General is honored in rank, you cannot fail to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Ji An, saying, "Since the emperor wishes the ministers to rank below the Grand General, and the Grand General is honored in rank, you cannot fail to bow.

sentences.zh: 」黯曰：「夫以大將軍，有揖客反不重邪！

translations.literal: " Ji An said: "For a Grand General to have a guest who bows with joined hands—would that not rather show honor!
translations.idiomatic: " Ji An said, "For a Grand General to have a guest who bows with joined hands—would that not rather show honor!

sentences.zh: 」大將軍聞，愈賢黯，數請問國家朝廷所疑，遇黯加於平日。

translations.literal: " When the Grand General heard this, he esteemed Ji An all the more, repeatedly asked him about what the state and court doubted, and treated Ji An even better than on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Grand General heard this, he esteemed Ji An all the more, repeatedly asked him about what the state and court doubted, and treated Ji An even better than on ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 大將軍青雖貴，有時侍中，上踞廁而視之；

translations.literal: Though Grand General Qing was honored, when he sometimes attended within the palace, the emperor would squat on the privy and look at him;
translations.idiomatic: Though Grand General Qing was honored, when he sometimes attended within the palace, the emperor would squat on the privy and look at him;

sentences.zh: 丞相弘燕見，上或時不冠；

translations.literal: when Chancellor Hong was received informally, the emperor sometimes went without his cap;
translations.idiomatic: when Chancellor Hong was received informally, the emperor sometimes went without his cap;

sentences.zh: 至如汲黯見，上不冠不見也。

translations.literal: but when it came to receiving Ji An, if the emperor was not capped he would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: but when it came to receiving Ji An, if the emperor was not capped he would not see him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗坐武帳中，黯前奏事，上不冠，望見黯，避帳中，使人可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor once sat in the military tent; Ji An came forward to report on affairs; the emperor was not capped; when he saw Ji An he withdrew within the tent and had someone approve his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sat in the military tent; Ji An came forward to report on affairs; the emperor was not capped; when he saw Ji An he withdrew within the tent and had someone approve his memorial.

sentences.zh: 其見敬禮如此。

translations.literal: The respect and ceremony shown him were like this.
translations.idiomatic: The respect and ceremony shown him were like this.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，六月，詔曰：「蓋聞導民以禮，風之以樂。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the sixth month, an edict said: "Your servant has heard that one guides the people with ritual and edifies them with music.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the sixth month, an edict said, "I have heard that one guides the people with ritual and edifies them with music.

sentences.zh: 今禮壞、樂崩，朕甚閔焉。

translations.literal: Now ritual is broken and music collapsed—We are deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Now ritual is broken and music collapsed—I am deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 其令禮官勸學興禮以為天下先！

translations.literal: Let the officials of ritual urge learning and raise ritual to be first for all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Let the officials of ritual urge learning and raise ritual to lead all under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」於是丞相弘等奏：「請為博士官置弟子五十人，復其身，第其高下，以補郎中、文學、掌故。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Chancellor Hong and others memorialized: "We request that fifty disciples be established for the Erudites' offices, that their persons be exempted, that they be ranked high and low, and that they be used to fill posts as Palace Gentlemen, literary officers, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Chancellor Hong and others memorialized, "We request fifty disciples for the Erudites' offices, exemption from corvée, ranking by merit, and appointment as Palace Gentlemen, literary officers, and clerks.

sentences.zh: 即有秀才異等，輒以名聞；

translations.literal: Whenever there are those of outstanding talent and unusual grade, report their names at once;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there are those of outstanding talent and unusual grade, report their names at once;

sentences.zh: 其不事學若下材，輒罷之。

translations.literal: those who do not pursue learning or are of inferior material, dismiss them at once.
translations.idiomatic: those who do not pursue learning or are of inferior material, dismiss them at once.

sentences.zh: 又，吏通一藝以上者，請皆選擇以補右職。

translations.literal: Moreover, among officials who are proficient in one art or more, we request that all be selected to fill right-hand posts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among officials proficient in one art or more, we request that all be selected to fill senior posts.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 自此公卿、大夫、士、吏彬彬多文學之士矣。

translations.literal: From this time forward, among high ministers, grandees, gentlemen, and clerks, many were refined and literary.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward, among high ministers, grandees, gentlemen, and clerks, many were refined and literary.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，匈奴萬騎入代，殺都尉朱英，略千餘人。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, ten thousand Xiongnu horsemen entered Dai, killed Commandant Zhu Ying, and carried off more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, ten thousand Xiongnu horsemen entered Dai, killed Commandant Zhu Ying, and carried off more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: ----6初，淮南王安，好讀書屬文，喜立名譽，招致賓客方術之士數千人。

translations.literal: ----6 At the outset, the Prince of Huainan, Liu An, loved reading books and composing texts, delighted in establishing reputation, and gathered several thousand guest retainers and masters of formulas and arts.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 At the outset, the Prince of Huainan, Liu An, loved reading and composing texts, delighted in making a name, and gathered several thousand guest retainers and masters of formulas and arts.

sentences.zh: 其群臣、賓客，多江、淮間輕薄士，常以厲王遷死感激安。

translations.literal: His ministers and guests were mostly frivolous gentlemen from between the Yangtze and Huai, who constantly stirred An's feelings with the death of King Li in exile.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers and guests were mostly frivolous gentlemen from between the Yangtze and Huai, who constantly stirred An's feelings with the death of King Li in exile.

sentences.zh: 建元六年，彗星見，或說王曰：「先吳軍時，彗星出，長數尺，然尚流血千里。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jianyuan a comet appeared; someone told the prince: "When the armies of Wu came first, a comet appeared several chi in length, yet still blood flowed for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jianyuan a comet appeared; someone told the prince, "When the armies of Wu rose first, a comet appeared several chi in length, yet still blood flowed for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 今彗星竟天，天下兵當大起。

translations.literal: Now the comet fills the sky—armies under Heaven will surely rise on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Now the comet fills the sky—armies under Heaven will surely rise on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 」王心以為然，乃益治攻戰具，積金錢。

translations.literal: " The prince's heart thought this true, and he thereupon increased his preparation of weapons for attack and defense and amassed gold and money.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince took this to heart, and thereupon increased his preparation of weapons for attack and defense and amassed gold and money.

sentences.zh: 郎中雷被獲罪於太子遷，時有詔，欲從軍者輒詣長安，被即願奮擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Lei Bei had offended the heir apparent Qian; at that time there was an edict that whoever wished to join the army should go at once to Chang'an—Bei immediately wished to strike the Xiongnu with fierce effort.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Lei Bei had offended the heir apparent Qian; at that time an edict said whoever wished to join the army should go at once to Chang'an—Bei immediately wished to strike the Xiongnu with all his might.

sentences.zh: 太子惡被於王，斥免之，欲以禁後。

translations.literal: The heir apparent hated Bei before the prince, dismissed and removed him, and wished thereby to forbid what might follow.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent hated Bei before the prince, dismissed and removed him, and wished thereby to forbid what might follow.

sentences.zh: 是歲，被亡之長安，上書自明。

translations.literal: That year Bei fled to Chang'an and memorialized to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Bei fled to Chang'an and memorialized to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 事下廷尉治，蹤跡連王，公卿請逮捕治王。

translations.literal: The affair was handed down to the Commandant of Justice for trial; the trail of evidence connected to the prince, and the high ministers requested that the prince be arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was handed down to the Commandant of Justice for trial; the trail of evidence connected to the prince, and the high ministers requested that the prince be arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 太子遷謀令人衣衛士衣，持戟居王旁，漢使有非是者，即刺殺之，因發兵反。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Qian plotted to have men dress in guards' clothing, hold halberds, and stand beside the prince; if any Han envoy did wrong, they were to stab and kill him at once and thereby raise troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Qian plotted to have men dress as guards, hold halberds, and stand beside the prince; if any Han envoy did wrong, they were to stab and kill him at once and thereby raise troops in revolt.

sentences.zh: 天子使中尉宏即訊王，王視中尉顏色和，遂不發。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Commandant of the Guards Hong to question the prince on the spot; the prince saw that the commandant's expression was mild and therefore did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Commandant of the Guards Hong to question the prince on the spot; the prince saw that the commandant's expression was mild and therefore did not rise.

sentences.zh: 公卿奏：「安壅閼奮擊匈奴者，格明詔，當棄市。

translations.literal: The high ministers memorialized: "An obstructed and blocked those who wished to strike the Xiongnu with fierce effort, resisted the clear edict, and should be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers memorialized, "An obstructed those who wished to strike the Xiongnu with all their might, resisted the clear edict, and should be executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 」詔削二縣。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered two counties stripped from his fief.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered two counties stripped from his fief.

sentences.zh: 既而安自傷曰：「吾行仁義，反見削地。

translations.literal: Afterward An wounded himself, saying: "I practiced benevolence and righteousness, yet in return my territory was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward An wounded himself, saying, "I practiced benevolence and righteousness, yet in return my territory was cut.

sentences.zh: 」恥之，於是為反謀益甚。

translations.literal: " He was shamed by this, and thereupon his plotting for revolt grew all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: " Shamed by this, he thereupon plotted revolt all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 安與衡山王賜相責望，禮節間不相能。

translations.literal: An and the Prince of Hengshan, Liu Ci, reproached and looked askance at each other; in ritual and courtesy they could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: An and the Prince of Hengshan, Liu Ci, reproached and looked askance at each other; in ritual and courtesy they could not get along.

sentences.zh: 衡山王聞淮南王有反謀，恐為所并，亦結賓客為反具，以為淮南已西，欲發兵定江、淮之間而有之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hengshan heard that the Prince of Huainan had a plot for revolt, feared being swallowed by him, and also gathered guests to prepare means of revolt, thinking that once Huainan was west of him he would raise troops, settle the region between the Yangtze and Huai, and possess it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hengshan heard that the Prince of Huainan plotted revolt, feared being swallowed by him, and also gathered guests to prepare for revolt, thinking that once Huainan lay to his west he would raise troops, settle the region between the Yangtze and Huai, and possess it.

sentences.zh: 衡山-{王后}-徐來譖太子爽於王，欲廢之而立其弟孝。

translations.literal: The -{王后}- of Hengshan, Xu Lai, slandered the heir apparent Shuang before the prince, wishing to depose him and establish his younger brother Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The -{王后}- of Hengshan, Xu Lai, slandered the heir apparent Shuang before the prince, wishing to depose him and establish his younger brother Xiao.

sentences.zh: 王囚太子而佩孝以王印，令招致賓客。

translations.literal: The prince imprisoned the heir apparent and hung the prince's seal on Xiao, ordering him to gather guests.
translations.idiomatic: The prince imprisoned the heir apparent and hung the prince's seal on Xiao, ordering him to gather guests.

sentences.zh: 賓客來者微知淮南、衡山有逆計，日夜從容勸之。

translations.literal: Guests who came gradually knew that Huainan and Hengshan had a rebellious plan and day and night, at ease, urged them on.
translations.idiomatic: Guests who came gradually learned that Huainan and Hengshan plotted rebellion and day and night, at their ease, urged them on.

sentences.zh: 王乃使孝客江都人枚赫、陳喜作輣車、鍛矢，刻天子璽、將相軍吏印。

translations.literal: The prince then had Xiao's guests, Mei He of Jiangdu and Chen Xi, make war chariots, forge arrows, and carve the Son of Heaven's seal and the seals of generals, ministers, and army officers.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then had Xiao's guests, Mei He of Jiangdu and Chen Xi, make war chariots, forge arrows, and carve the emperor's seal and the seals of generals, ministers, and army officers.

sentences.zh: 秋，衡山王當入朝，過淮南；

translations.literal: In autumn, when the Prince of Hengshan was to enter court and passed through Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, when the Prince of Hengshan was to enter court and passed through Huainan;

sentences.zh: 淮南王乃昆弟語，除前隙，約束反具。

translations.literal: the Prince of Huainan then spoke with him as brothers, removed their former rift, and agreed on their means of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Huainan spoke with him as brothers, removed their former rift, and agreed on their means of revolt.

sentences.zh: 衡山王即上書謝病，上賜書不朝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hengshan at once memorialized to plead illness; the emperor granted a letter excusing him from court.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hengshan at once memorialized to plead illness; the emperor granted a letter excusing him from court.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，大將軍青出定襄，擊匈奴；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the second month, Grand General Qing marched out from Dingxiang to strike the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the second month, Grand General Qing marched out from Dingxiang to strike the Xiongnu;

sentences.zh: 以合騎侯公孫敖為中將軍，太僕公孫賀為左將軍，翕侯趙信為前將軍，衛尉蘇建為右將軍，郎中令李廣為後將軍，左內史李沮為強弩將軍，咸屬大將軍。

translations.literal: Marquis of Heqi Gongsun Ao was made Lieutenant General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He was made Left General, Marquis of Xi Zhao Xin was made Forward General, Commandant of the Guard Su Jian was made Right General, Director of the Secretariat Li Guang was made Rear General, and Left Metropolitan Steward Li Ju was made Powerful Crossbow General—all were placed under the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Heqi Gongsun Ao was made Lieutenant General, Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He Left General, Marquis of Xi Zhao Xin Forward General, Commandant of the Guard Su Jian Right General, Director of the Secretariat Li Guang Rear General, and Left Metropolitan Steward Li Ju Powerful Crossbow General—all under the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 斬首數千級而還，休士馬於定襄、雲中、雁門。

translations.literal: They beheaded several thousand and returned, resting men and horses at Dingxiang, Yunzhong, and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded several thousand and returned, resting men and horses at Dingxiang, Yunzhong, and Yanmen.

translations.literal: ----2 There was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 There was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----3夏，四月，衛青復將六將軍出定襄，擊匈奴，斬首虜萬餘人。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, Wei Qing again led the six generals out from Dingxiang to strike the Xiongnu and beheaded and captured more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, Wei Qing again led the six generals out from Dingxiang to strike the Xiongnu and beheaded and captured more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 右將軍建、前將軍信並軍三千餘騎獨逢單于兵，與戰一日餘，漢兵且盡。

translations.literal: Right General Jian and Forward General Xin combined their armies—more than three thousand horsemen—and alone encountered the chanyu's troops; they fought for more than a day, and the Han troops were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Right General Jian and Forward General Xin combined their armies—more than three thousand horsemen—and alone encountered the chanyu's troops; they fought for more than a day, and the Han troops were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 信故胡小王，降漢，漢封為翕侯，及敗，匈奴誘之，遂將其餘騎可八百降匈奴。

translations.literal: Xin had formerly been a minor king of the Hu; he surrendered to Han and Han enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xi; when defeated, the Xiongnu lured him, and he thereupon led his remaining horsemen, about eight hundred, to surrender to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had formerly been a minor king of the Hu; he surrendered to Han and Han enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xi; when defeated, the Xiongnu lured him, and he led his remaining horsemen, about eight hundred, to surrender to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 建盡亡其軍，脫身亡，自歸大將軍。

translations.literal: Jian completely lost his army, escaped alive, and returned on his own to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Jian lost his entire army, escaped alive, and returned on his own to the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 議郎周霸曰：「自大將軍出，未嘗斬裨將。

translations.literal: Palace Counselor Zhou Ba said: "Since the Grand General marched out, he has never beheaded a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Counselor Zhou Ba said, "Since the Grand General marched out, he has never beheaded a subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 今建棄軍，可斬，以明將軍之威。

translations.literal: Now Jian abandoned his army—he may be beheaded to make clear the general's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jian abandoned his army—he should be beheaded to make clear the general's majesty.

sentences.zh: 」軍正閎、長史安曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Army Rectifier Hong and Chief Clerk An said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Army Rectifier Hong and Chief Clerk An said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》：『小敵之堅，大敵之禽也。

translations.literal: The Art of War: 'When a small enemy is obstinate, a great enemy takes him.'
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says, 'When a small enemy is obstinate, a great enemy takes him.'

sentences.zh: 』今建以數千當單于數萬，力戰一日餘，士盡，不敢有二心，自歸，而斬之，是示後無反意也，不當斬。

translations.literal: 』 Now Jian with several thousand faced the Chanyu's tens of thousands, fought fiercely for more than a day until the soldiers were exhausted, dared not harbor a second thought, and surrendered of himself—yet to execute him is to show posterity there is no intent of returning; he ought not to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: 』 Now Jian with several thousand faced the Chanyu's tens of thousands, fought fiercely for more than a day until his men were spent, dared not harbor a second thought, and surrendered of his own accord—yet to execute him is to show those who follow that there is no point in returning; he ought not to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 」大將軍曰：「青幸得以肺腑待罪行間，不患無威，而霸說我以明威，甚失臣意。

translations.literal: 」 The Great General said: "Having been fortunate to serve among capital offenders with the emperor's close trust, I do not worry about lacking authority, yet Ba urges me to display authority clearly—this greatly misses the intent of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The Great General said, "Having been fortunate to serve among capital offenders with the emperor's close trust, I do not worry about lacking authority, yet Ba urges me to display authority clearly—this greatly misses what a subject ought to do.

sentences.zh: 且使臣職雖當斬將，以臣之尊寵而不敢擅誅於境外，而具歸天子，天子自裁之，於以見為人臣不敢專權，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, though my office might require executing a general, given my honored favor I dare not execute on my own authority beyond the borders, but should present him complete to the Son of Heaven for the Son of Heaven to judge—thereby showing that as a subject one dare not monopolize authority—is that not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though my office might require executing a general, given my honored favor I dare not put him to death on my own authority beyond the borders, but should present him intact to the Son of Heaven for the Son of Heaven to judge—thereby showing that as a subject one dare not monopolize authority—is that not acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」軍吏皆曰：「善！

translations.literal: 」 The army officers all said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: 」 The army officers all said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」遂囚建詣行在所。

translations.literal: 」 They then imprisoned Jian and brought him to the emperor's traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: 」 They then imprisoned Jian and brought him to the emperor's traveling residence.

sentences.zh: 初，平陽縣吏霍仲孺給事平陽侯家，與青姊衛少兒私通，生霍去病。

translations.literal: At the outset, Pingyang county clerk Huo Zhongru served in the household of the Marquis of Pingyang, had a secret liaison with Wei's younger sister Wei Shao'er, and fathered Huo Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Pingyang county clerk Huo Zhongru served in the household of the Marquis of Pingyang, had a secret liaison with Wei's younger sister Wei Shao'er, and fathered Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 去病年十八，為侍中，善騎射，再從大將軍擊匈奴，為嫖姚校尉，與輕騎勇八百，直棄大軍數百里赴利，斬捕首虜過當。

translations.literal: Qubing at eighteen was a palace attendant, skilled in mounted archery, and again followed the Great General in attacking the Xiongnu as Colonel of Swift Cavalry; with eight hundred light horsemen of courage he straightway left the main army several hundred li to seize gain, and beheaded and captured enemy heads and prisoners beyond the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing at eighteen was a palace attendant, skilled in mounted archery, and again followed the Great General in attacking the Xiongnu as Colonel of Swift Cavalry; with eight hundred light horsemen of courage he straightway left the main army several hundred li to seize gain, and beheaded and captured enemy heads and prisoners beyond the quota.

sentences.zh: 於是天子曰：「嫖姚校尉去病，斬首虜二千餘級，得相國、當戶，斬單于大父行藉若侯產，生捕季父羅姑，比再冠軍，封去病為冠軍侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven said: "Colonel of Swift Cavalry Qubing beheaded over two thousand enemy heads and prisoners, captured the Xiangguo and Danghu, slew the Chanyu's grandfather's rank Jieruo Marquis Chan, and took alive the younger paternal uncle Luo Gu; comparable to twice being champion—Qubing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor said, "Colonel of Swift Cavalry Qubing beheaded over two thousand enemy heads and prisoners, captured the Xiangguo and Danghu, slew the Chanyu's grandfather's rank Jieruo Marquis Chan, and took alive the younger paternal uncle Luo Gu; comparable to twice being champion—Qubing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Champion.

sentences.zh: 上谷太守郝賢四從大將軍，捕斬首虜二千餘級，封賢為眾利侯。

translations.literal: Shanggu Administrator Hao Xian four times followed the Great General, captured and beheaded over two thousand enemy heads and prisoners, and Xian was enfeoffed as Marquis of All Profit.
translations.idiomatic: Shanggu Administrator Hao Xian four times followed the Great General, captured and beheaded over two thousand enemy heads and prisoners, and Xian was enfeoffed as Marquis of All Profit.

sentences.zh: 是歲，失兩將軍，亡翕侯，軍功不多，故大將軍不益封，止賜千金。

translations.literal: That year two generals were lost and the Marquis of Harmony fled; military achievement was not great, so the Great General received no added enfeoffment and was granted only a thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: That year two generals were lost and the Marquis of Harmony defected; military achievement was not great, so the Great General received no added enfeoffment and was granted only a thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 右將軍建至，天子不誅，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: When General of the Right Jian arrived, the Son of Heaven did not execute him but ransomed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When General of the Right Jian arrived, the emperor did not execute him but ransomed him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 單于既得翕侯，以為自次王，用其姊妻之，與謀漢。

translations.literal: Once the Chanyu had obtained the Marquis of Harmony, he made him his own secondary king, married him to the Chanyu's elder sister, and plotted against Han with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Chanyu had obtained the Marquis of Harmony, he made him his own secondary king, married him to the Chanyu's elder sister, and plotted against Han with him.

sentences.zh: 信教單于益北絕幕，以誘罷漢兵，徼極而取之，無近塞。

translations.literal: Xin instructed the Chanyu to move further north beyond the desert curtain to lure and wear out Han troops, wait until they reached extremity and then take them, and not approach the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xin instructed the Chanyu to move further north beyond the desert curtain to lure and wear out Han troops, wait until they reached extremity and then take them, and not approach the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 單于從其計。

translations.literal: The Chanyu followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢比歲發十餘萬眾擊胡，斬捕首虜之士受賜黃金二十餘萬斤，而漢軍士馬死者十餘萬，兵甲轉漕之費不與焉。

translations.literal: At that time Han year after year sent out over a hundred thousand men to attack the Hu; soldiers who beheaded and captured heads and prisoners received grants of gold totaling over two hundred thousand jin, while Han army soldiers and horses who died numbered over a hundred thousand—the costs of armor, weapons, and transport were not included.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han year after year sent out over a hundred thousand men to attack the Hu; soldiers who beheaded and captured heads and prisoners received grants of gold totaling over two hundred thousand jin, while Han army soldiers and horses who died numbered over a hundred thousand—the costs of armor, weapons, and transport were not included.

sentences.zh: 於是大司農經用竭，不足以奉戰士。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Minister of Agriculture's regular expenditures were exhausted and insufficient to supply the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Grand Minister of Agriculture's regular expenditures were exhausted and insufficient to supply the warriors.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔令民得買爵及贖禁錮，免臧罪。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict allowed the people to buy noble ranks and redeem imprisonment, exempting capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, an edict allowed the people to buy noble ranks and redeem imprisonment, exempting capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 置賞官，名曰武功爵，級十七萬，凡直三十餘萬金。

translations.literal: Reward offices were established, named Martial Achievement Nobility, seventeen grades in all, altogether worth more than three hundred thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Reward offices were established, named Martial Achievement Nobility, with seventeen grades in all, altogether worth more than three hundred thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 諸買武功爵至千夫者，得先除為吏。

translations.literal: All who bought Martial Achievement nobility up to the rank of Thousand Husband could be appointed as clerks ahead of others.
translations.idiomatic: All who bought Martial Achievement nobility up to the rank of Thousand Husband could be appointed as clerks ahead of others.

sentences.zh: 吏道雜而多端，官職耗廢矣。

translations.literal: The path of office became complex and many-sided; official posts were worn out and wasted.
translations.idiomatic: The path of office became complex and many-sided; official posts were worn out and wasted.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上行幸雍，祠五畤，獲獸，一角而足有五蹄。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong, sacrificed at the Five Altars, and obtained a beast with one horn and feet having five hooves.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong, sacrificed at the Five Altars, and obtained a beast with one horn and feet having five hooves.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「陛下肅祗郊祀，上帝報享，錫一角獸，蓋麟雲。

translations.literal: The responsible officials said: "Your Majesty reverently performed suburban sacrifice; the Supreme Lord responded with enjoyment and bestowed a one-horned beast—perhaps a qilin.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials said, "Your Majesty reverently performed suburban sacrifice; the Supreme Lord responded with enjoyment and bestowed a one-horned beast—perhaps a qilin.

sentences.zh: 」於是以慶五畤，畤加一牛，以燎。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he celebrated at the Five Altars, adding one ox to each altar, and burned them as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he celebrated at the Five Altars, adding one ox to each altar, and burned them as offerings.

sentences.zh: 久之，有司又言：「元宜以天瑞命，不宜以一二數，一元曰建，二元以長星曰光，今元以郊得一角獸曰狩雲。

translations.literal: After some time the responsible officials again said: "The era name ought to be taken from heavenly omens, not from one or two counts; the first era was called Jian, the second, from the long star, was called Guang; now the era, from obtaining a one-horned beast at the suburban sacrifice, should be called Shouyun.
translations.idiomatic: After some time the responsible officials again said, "The era name ought to be taken from heavenly omens, not from one or two counts; the first era was called Jian, the second, from the long star, was called Guang; now the era, from obtaining a one-horned beast at the suburban sacrifice, should be called Shouyun.

sentences.zh: 」於是濟北王以為天子且封禪，上書獻太山及其旁邑。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Prince of Jibei, thinking the Son of Heaven was about to perform the Feng and Shan rites, memorialized offering Mount Tai and the neighboring towns.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Prince of Jibei, thinking the emperor was about to perform the Feng and Shan rites, memorialized offering Mount Tai and the neighboring towns.

sentences.zh: 天子以他縣償之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven compensated him with other counties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor compensated him with other counties.

sentences.zh: ----2淮南王安與賓客左吳等日夜為反謀，按輿地圖，部署兵所從入。

translations.literal: ----2 King An of Huainan and his retainers Zuo Wu and others day and night made rebellion plans, consulted the geographical maps, and deployed where troops would enter.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 King An of Huainan and his retainers Zuo Wu and others day and night made rebellion plans, consulted the geographical maps, and deployed where troops would enter.

sentences.zh: 諸使者道長安來，為妄言，言「上無男，漢不治」，即喜；

translations.literal: Envoys coming by the road from Chang'an spoke reckless words, saying "The emperor has no sons; Han will not endure"—then he rejoiced;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys coming by the road from Chang'an spoke reckless words, saying "The emperor has no sons; Han will not endure"—then he rejoiced;

sentences.zh: 即言「漢廷治，有男」，王怒，以為妄言，非也。

translations.literal: when they spoke "The Han court endures; there is a son," the king was angry and took it as reckless talk, not true.
translations.idiomatic: when they spoke "The Han court endures; there is a son," the king was angry and took it as reckless talk, not true.

sentences.zh: 王召中郎伍被與謀反事，被曰：「王安得此亡國之言乎？

translations.literal: The king summoned Palace Gentleman Wu Bei to discuss rebellion; Bei said: "How does Your Majesty obtain such state-destroying words?
translations.idiomatic: The king summoned Palace Gentleman Wu Bei to discuss rebellion; Bei said, "How does Your Majesty obtain such state-destroying words?

sentences.zh: 臣見宮中生荊棘，露霑衣也。

translations.literal: I see brambles growing in the palace and dew soaking one's robes.
translations.idiomatic: I see brambles growing in the palace and dew soaking one's robes.

sentences.zh: 」王怒，系伍被父母，囚之。

translations.literal: " The king was angry, seized Wu Bei's parents, and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: " The king was angry, seized Wu Bei's parents, and imprisoned them.

sentences.zh: 三月，復召問之，被曰：「昔秦為無道，窮奢極虐，百姓思亂者十家而六七。

translations.literal: In the third month he summoned and questioned him again; Bei said: "Formerly Qin was without the Way, exhausting luxury and reaching the utmost in cruelty; of the common people, six or seven in ten households wished for disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he summoned and questioned him again; Bei said, "Formerly Qin was without the Way, exhausting luxury and reaching the utmost in cruelty; of the common people, six or seven in ten households wished for disorder.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝起於行陳之中，立為天子，此所謂蹈瑕候間，因秦之亡而動者也。

translations.literal: The High Emperor rose from within the battle ranks and was established as Son of Heaven—this is what is called treading a flaw and watching for an opening, moving because Qin was perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor rose from within the battle ranks and was established as emperor—this is what is called treading a flaw and watching for an opening, moving because Qin was perishing.

sentences.zh: 今大王見高皇帝得天下之易也，獨不觀近世之吳、楚乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty sees how easily the High Emperor obtained all under Heaven—will you alone not observe the recent cases of Wu and Chu!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty sees how easily the High Emperor obtained all under Heaven—will you alone not observe the recent cases of Wu and Chu!

sentences.zh: 夫吳王王四郡，國富民眾，計定謀成，舉兵而西；

translations.literal: The King of Wu ruled four commanderies, the state was rich and the people numerous, plans were settled and schemes completed, and he raised troops and marched west;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu ruled four commanderies, the state was rich and the people numerous, plans were settled and schemes completed, and he raised troops and marched west;

sentences.zh: 然破於大梁，奔走而東，身死祀絕者何？

translations.literal: yet he was broken at Daliang, fled east, and his person died and sacrifices ended—why?
translations.idiomatic: yet he was broken at Daliang, fled east, and his person died and sacrifices ended—why?

sentences.zh: 誠逆天道而不知時也。

translations.literal: Truly he opposed Heaven's Way and did not know the times.
translations.idiomatic: Truly he opposed Heaven's Way and did not know the times.

sentences.zh: 方今大王之兵，眾不能十分吳、楚之一，天下安寧，萬倍吳、楚之時，大王不從臣之計，今見大王棄千乘之君，賜絕命之書，為群臣先死於東宮也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's troops in number cannot reach one-tenth of Wu and Chu's; all under Heaven is tranquil, ten thousand times the time of Wu and Chu—if Your Majesty does not follow my plan, I now see Your Majesty abandoning a lord of a thousand chariots, bestowing a letter of severed fate, and going before the ministers to die in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's troops in number cannot reach one-tenth of Wu and Chu's; all under Heaven is tranquil, ten thousand times the time of Wu and Chu—if Your Majesty does not follow my plan, I now see Your Majesty abandoning a lord of a thousand chariots, bestowing a letter of severed fate, and going before the ministers to die in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 」王涕泣而起。

translations.literal: " The king wept and rose.
translations.idiomatic: " The king wept and rose.

sentences.zh: 王有孽子不害，最長，王弗愛，王后、太子皆不以為子、兄數。

translations.literal: The king had an illegitimate son Buhai, the eldest; the king did not love him, and the queen and crown prince both did not treat him with the count due a son or elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The king had an illegitimate son Buhai, the eldest; the king did not love him, and the queen and crown prince both did not treat him with the count due a son or elder brother.

sentences.zh: 不害有子建，材高有氣，常怨望太子，陰使人告太子謀殺漢中尉事，下廷尉治。

translations.literal: Buhai had a son Jian, talented and high-spirited, who constantly resented and looked askance at the crown prince; he secretly sent men to accuse the crown prince of plotting to kill the Commandant of Hanzhong, and the case was sent down to the Court Commandant for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai had a son Jian, talented and high-spirited, who constantly resented and looked askance at the crown prince; he secretly sent men to accuse the crown prince of plotting to kill the Commandant of Hanzhong, and the case was sent down to the Court Commandant for judgment.

sentences.zh: 王患之，欲發，復問伍被曰：「公以為吳興兵，是邪？

translations.literal: The king was troubled by this and wished to rise in revolt; he again asked Wu Bei, saying: "Do you think Wu's raising troops was right?
translations.idiomatic: The king was troubled by this and wished to rise in revolt; he again asked Wu Bei, saying, "Do you think Wu's raising troops was right?

sentences.zh: 非邪？

translations.literal: Or not?
translations.idiomatic: Or not?

sentences.zh: 」被曰：「非也。

translations.literal: " Bei said: "It was not.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei said, "It was not.

sentences.zh: 臣聞吳王悔之甚，願王無為吳王之所悔。

translations.literal: I have heard the King of Wu regretted it deeply; I wish Your Majesty not to do what the King of Wu regretted.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the King of Wu regretted it deeply; I wish Your Majesty not to do what the King of Wu regretted.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「吳何知反！

translations.literal: " The king said: "How would Wu know to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "How would Wu know to rebel!

sentences.zh: 漢將一日過成皋者四十餘人，今我絕成皋之口，據三川之險，招山東之兵，舉事如此，左吳、趙賢、朱驕如皆以為什事九成，公獨以為有禍無福，何也？

translations.literal: In one day over forty Han generals passed through Chenggao; now if I cut off the mouth of Chenggao, hold the peril of the Three Rivers, recruit the troops of Shandong, and raise the affair thus—Zuo Wu, Zhao Xian, Zhu Jiaoru all think nine-tenths of ten things assured, yet you alone think there is misfortune without blessing—why?
translations.idiomatic: In one day over forty Han generals passed through Chenggao; now if I cut off the mouth of Chenggao, hold the peril of the Three Rivers, recruit the troops of Shandong, and raise the affair thus—Zuo Wu, Zhao Xian, Zhu Jiaoru all think nine-tenths of ten things assured, yet you alone think there is misfortune without blessing—why?

sentences.zh: 必如公言，不可徼幸邪？

translations.literal: If it must be as you say, may one not hope for good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: If it must be as you say, may one not hope for good fortune?

sentences.zh: 」被曰：「必不得已，被有愚計。

translations.literal: " Bei said: "If it must be done, Bei has a foolish plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei said, "If it must be done, Bei has a foolish plan.

sentences.zh: 當今諸侯無異心，百姓無怨氣，可偽為丞相、御史請書，徙郡國豪桀高貲於朔方，益發甲卒，急其會日；

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords have no divergent hearts and the common people have no resentment; one may forge a memorial from the Chancellor and Imperial Secretary requesting to relocate the powerful and wealthy of the commanderies and kingdoms to Shuofang, increase the dispatch of armored soldiers, and hurry the assembly date;
translations.idiomatic: Now the feudal lords have no divergent hearts and the common people have no resentment; one may forge a memorial from the Chancellor and Imperial Secretary requesting to relocate the powerful and wealthy of the commanderies and kingdoms to Shuofang, increase the dispatch of armored soldiers, and hurry the assembly date;

sentences.zh: 又偽為詔獄書，逮諸侯太子、幸臣。

translations.literal: also forge an imperial prison edict arresting the crown princes and favored ministers of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: also forge an imperial prison edict arresting the crown princes and favored ministers of the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 如此，則民怨，諸侯懼，即使辯士隨而說之，儻可徼幸什得一乎！

translations.literal: If so, the people will resent and the feudal lords will fear; then even if persuasive scholars follow to speak to them, perhaps one might hope for good fortune and get one in ten!
translations.idiomatic: If so, the people will resent and the feudal lords will fear; then even if persuasive scholars follow to speak to them, perhaps one might hope for good fortune and get one in ten!

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「此可也。

translations.literal: " The king said: "This will do.
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "This will do.

sentences.zh: 雖然，吾以為不至若此。

translations.literal: Even so, I think it will not come to that.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I think it will not come to that.

sentences.zh: 於是王乃作皇帝璽，丞相、御史大夫、將軍、軍吏、中二千石及旁近郡太守、都尉印，漢使節。

translations.literal: Thereupon the king made the emperor's seal, seals of Chancellor, Grand Secretary, generals, army officers, officials of two-thousand-dan rank and above, and the administrators and commandants of neighboring commanderies, and Han envoy credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the king made the emperor's seal, seals of Chancellor, Grand Secretary, generals, army officers, officials of two-thousand-dan rank and above, and the administrators and commandants of neighboring commanderies, and Han envoy credentials.

sentences.zh: 欲使人偽得罪而西，事大將軍，一日發兵，即刺殺大將軍。

translations.literal: He wished to send men who would feign guilt and go west to serve the Great General, and on the day troops were raised immediately assassinate the Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to send men who would feign guilt and go west to serve the Great General, and on the day troops were raised immediately assassinate the Great General.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「漢廷大臣，獨汲黯好直諫，守節死義，難惑以非；

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "Among Han court great ministers, only Ji An loves straight remonstrance and keeps his integrity unto death in righteousness—hard to confuse with wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he said, "Among Han court great ministers, only Ji An loves straight remonstrance and keeps his integrity unto death in righteousness—hard to confuse with wrong;

sentences.zh: 至如說丞相弘等，如發蒙振落耳！

translations.literal: but as for persuading the Chancellor Hong and the rest, it would be like lifting a blindfold and shaking off fallen leaves!
translations.idiomatic: but as for persuading the Chancellor Hong and the rest, it would be like lifting a blindfold and shaking off fallen leaves!

sentences.zh: 王欲發國中兵，恐其相、二千石不聽，王乃與伍被謀先殺相、二千石。

translations.literal: The king wished to mobilize troops within the state but feared the Chancellor and the two-thousand-dan officials would not obey; the king then plotted with Wu Bei first to kill the Chancellor and the two-thousand-dan officials.
translations.idiomatic: The king wished to mobilize troops within the state but feared the Chancellor and the two-thousand-dan officials would not obey; the king then plotted with Wu Bei first to kill the Chancellor and the two-thousand-dan officials.

sentences.zh: 又欲令人衣求盜衣，持羽檄從東方來，呼曰：「南越兵入界！

translations.literal: He also wished to have men dress in robber-seeking garb, hold feather dispatch slips coming from the east, and cry: "Southern Yue troops have crossed the border!
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to have men dress in robber-seeking garb, hold feather dispatch slips coming from the east, and cry, "Southern Yue troops have crossed the border!

sentences.zh: 」欲因以發兵。

translations.literal: " intending thereby to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: " intending thereby to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 會廷尉逮捕淮南太子，淮南王聞之，與太子謀，召相、二千石，欲殺而發兵。

translations.literal: Just then the Court Commandant arrested the crown prince of Huainan; when the King of Huainan heard, he plotted with the crown prince, summoned the Chancellor and two-thousand-dan officials, and wished to kill them and raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Court Commandant arrested the crown prince of Huainan; when the King of Huainan heard, he plotted with the crown prince, summoned the Chancellor and two-thousand-dan officials, and wished to kill them and raise troops.

sentences.zh: 召相，相至，內史、中尉皆不至。

translations.literal: He summoned the Chancellor; the Chancellor arrived, but the Inner Scribe and Commandant of the Guards both did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the Chancellor; the Chancellor arrived, but the Inner Scribe and Commandant of the Guards both did not come.

sentences.zh: 王念，獨殺相無益也，即罷相。

translations.literal: The king reflected that killing the Chancellor alone would be of no use and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The king reflected that killing the Chancellor alone would be of no use and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 王猶豫，計未決。

translations.literal: The king hesitated and his plan was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: The king hesitated and his plan was not settled.

sentences.zh: 太子即自剄，不殊。

translations.literal: The crown prince immediately cut his own throat but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince immediately cut his own throat but did not die.

sentences.zh: 伍被自詣吏，告與淮南王謀反蹤跡如此。

translations.literal: Wu Bei went on his own to the officials and reported the traces of his rebellion plotting with the King of Huainan as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bei went on his own to the officials and reported the traces of his rebellion plotting with the King of Huainan as follows.

sentences.zh: 吏因捕太子、王后，圍王宮，盡求捕王所與謀反賓客在國中者，索得反具，以上。

translations.literal: The officials thereupon arrested the crown prince and queen, surrounded the royal palace, thoroughly sought and arrested within the state all the king's retainers who had plotted rebellion with him, obtained the rebel equipment, and presented it above.
translations.idiomatic: The officials thereupon arrested the crown prince and queen, surrounded the royal palace, thoroughly sought and arrested within the state all the king's retainers who had plotted rebellion with him, obtained the rebel equipment, and presented it above.

sentences.zh: 下公卿治其黨與，使宗正以符節治王。

translations.literal: The case was sent down to the excellencies and ministers to judge his cliques and associates, and the Director of the Imperial Clan was sent with credentials to judge the king.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent down to the excellencies and ministers to judge his cliques and associates, and the Director of the Imperial Clan was sent with credentials to judge the king.

sentences.zh: 未至，淮南王安自剄。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, King An of Huainan cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, King An of Huainan cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 殺王后荼、太子遷，諸所與謀反者皆族。

translations.literal: Queen Cha, Crown Prince Qian, and all who had plotted rebellion with him were executed and their clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Cha, Crown Prince Qian, and all who had plotted rebellion with him were executed and their clans exterminated.

sentences.zh: 天子以伍被雅辭多引漢之美，欲勿誅。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because Wu Bei's elegant words often cited Han's excellence, wished not to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Wu Bei's elegant words often cited Han's excellence, wished not to execute him.

sentences.zh: 廷尉湯曰：「被首為王畫反計，罪不可赦。

translations.literal: Court Commandant Tang said: "Bei was the first to draw up rebellion plans for the king; the crime cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Court Commandant Tang said, "Bei was the first to draw up rebellion plans for the king; the crime cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」乃誅被。

translations.literal: " Bei was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Bei was then executed.

sentences.zh: 侍中莊助素與淮南王相結交，私論議，王厚賂遺助；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhuang Zhu had long been friendly with the King of Huainan, discussed matters in private, and the king richly bribed and sent him gifts;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhuang Zhu had long been friendly with the King of Huainan, discussed matters in private, and the king richly bribed and sent him gifts;

sentences.zh: 上薄其罪，欲勿誅。

translations.literal: the emperor lightened his crime and wished not to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor lightened his crime and wished not to execute him.

sentences.zh: 張湯爭，以為：「助出入禁門，腹心之臣，而外與諸侯交私如此，不誅，後不可治。

translations.literal: Zhang Tang disputed, holding: "Zhu went in and out of the forbidden gates as a bosom-and-belly minister, yet privately associated with feudal lords like this—if not executed, later it cannot be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tang disputed, holding, "Zhu went in and out of the forbidden gates as a bosom-and-belly minister, yet privately associated with feudal lords like this—if not executed, later it cannot be governed.

sentences.zh: 」助竟棄市。

translations.literal: " Zhu was finally executed at the market.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu was finally executed at the market.

sentences.zh: 衡山王上書，請廢太子爽，立其弟孝為太子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hengshan memorialized requesting to depose Crown Prince Shuang and establish his younger brother Xiao as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hengshan memorialized requesting to depose Crown Prince Shuang and establish his younger brother Xiao as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 爽聞，即遣所善白嬴之長安上書，言「孝作輣車、鍛矢，與王御者奸」，欲以敗孝。

translations.literal: Shuang heard and immediately sent his favorite Bai Ying to Chang'an to memorialize, saying "Xiao makes armored wagons and forges arrows and has illicit relations with the king's charioteer," intending thereby to ruin Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang heard and immediately sent his favorite Bai Ying to Chang'an to memorialize, saying "Xiao makes armored wagons and forges arrows and has illicit relations with the king's charioteer," intending thereby to ruin Xiao.

sentences.zh: 會有司捕所與淮南謀反者，得陳喜於衡山王子孝家，吏劾孝首匿喜。

translations.literal: Just then the responsible officials were arresting those who had plotted rebellion with Huainan; Chen Xi was found in the home of the Prince of Hengshan's son Xiao, and the clerks impeached Xiao for first concealing Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the responsible officials were arresting those who had plotted rebellion with Huainan; Chen Xi was found in the home of the Prince of Hengshan's son Xiao, and the clerks impeached Xiao for first concealing Xi.

sentences.zh: 孝聞「律：先自告，除其罪」，即先自告所與謀反者枚赫、陳喜等。

translations.literal: Xiao heard "The law: whoever first reports himself is exempted from his crime," and immediately first reported himself concerning those who had plotted rebellion with him—Mei He, Chen Xi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao heard "The law: whoever first reports himself is exempted from his crime," and immediately first reported himself concerning those who had plotted rebellion with him—Mei He, Chen Xi, and others.

sentences.zh: 公卿請逮捕衡山王治之，王自剄死。

translations.literal: The excellencies and ministers requested arresting the Prince of Hengshan to judge him; the king cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: The excellencies and ministers requested arresting the Prince of Hengshan to judge him; the king cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 王后徐來、太子爽及孝皆棄市，所與謀反者皆族。

translations.literal: Queen Xu Lai, Crown Prince Shuang, and Xiao were all executed at the market; those who had plotted rebellion with them were all clan-exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Xu Lai, Crown Prince Shuang, and Xiao were all executed at the market; those who had plotted rebellion with them were all clan-exterminated.

sentences.zh: 凡淮南、衡山二獄，所連引列侯、二千石、豪桀等，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: In all, in the two cases of Huainan and Hengshan, those implicated and drawn in—marquises, two-thousand-dan officials, powerful men, and the like—who died numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In all, in the two cases of Huainan and Hengshan, those implicated and drawn in—marquises, two-thousand-dan officials, powerful men, and the like—who died numbered tens of thousands.

translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

translations.idiomatic: ----4 On dingmao, the emperor's son Ju was established as crown prince, aged seven.

translations.literal: ----5 In the fifth month, on the last day of yisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the fifth month, on the last day of yisi, there was a solar eclipse.

translations.idiomatic: ----6 Ten thousand Xiongnu entered Shanggu and killed several hundred people.

translations.idiomatic: ----7 At the outset, Zhang Qian returned from the Yuezhi and fully reported to the emperor the customs of the Western Region states: "Dayuan lies due west of Han, perhaps ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其俗土著，耕田；

translations.literal: Their custom is settled on the soil and plowing fields;
translations.idiomatic: Their custom is settled on the soil and plowing fields;

sentences.zh: 多善馬，馬汗血；

translations.literal: they have many good horses, horses that sweat blood;
translations.idiomatic: they have many good horses, horses that sweat blood;

translations.literal: they have ramparts, walls, and houses like the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: they have ramparts, walls, and houses like the Middle Kingdom.

translations.idiomatic: To their northeast is Wusun; to the east is -{于窴}-.

translations.idiomatic: West of -{于窴}-, all waters flow west and enter the Western Sea; east of it, waters flow east and enter the Salt Marsh.

translations.literal: The Salt Marsh runs underground; south of it the Yellow River's source emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt Marsh runs underground; south of it the Yellow River's source emerges.

sentences.zh: 鹽澤去長安可五千里。

translations.literal: The Salt Marsh is perhaps five thousand li from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt Marsh is perhaps five thousand li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 匈奴右方居鹽澤以東，至隴西長城，南接羌，鬲漢道焉。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu right wing dwells east of the Salt Marsh to the Longxi Wall, south connecting with the Qiang, blocking the Han road.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu right wing dwells east of the Salt Marsh to the Longxi Wall, south connecting with the Qiang, blocking the Han road.

translations.literal: Wusun, Kangju, Yancai, and the Great Yuezhi are all traveling states, following their herds in pasture, of the same custom as the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun, Kangju, Yancai, and the Great Yuezhi are all traveling states, following their herds in pasture, of the same custom as the Xiongnu.

translations.literal: Da Xia is southwest of Dayuan, same customs as Dayuan.

translations.idiomatic: When your servant was in Bactria, he saw Qiong bamboo staffs and Shu cloth and asked, 'How did you obtain these?

sentences.zh: 』大夏國人曰：『吾賈人往市之身毒。

translations.literal: ' The people of Da Xia said: 'Our traders go to market in Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: ' The people of Bactria said, 'Our merchants go to trade in India (Shendu).

sentences.zh: 』身毒在大夏東南可數千里，其俗土著，與大夏同。

translations.literal: ' Shendu is southeast of Da Xia perhaps several thousand li; their custom is to settle on the land, same as Da Xia.
translations.idiomatic: ' India lies several thousand li southeast of Bactria; the people are sedentary, and their customs are the same as Bactria's.

sentences.zh: 以騫度之，大夏去漢萬二千里，居漢西南；

translations.literal: By Qian's estimate, Da Xia is twelve thousand li from Han, located southwest of Han;
translations.idiomatic: By Zhang Qian's estimate, Bactria is twelve thousand li from Han and lies southwest of Han;

sentences.zh: 今身毒國又居大夏東南數千里，有蜀物，此其去蜀不遠矣。

translations.literal: Now Shendu also dwells several thousand li southeast of Da Xia, has Shu goods—this shows it is not far from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Now India also lies several thousand li southeast of Bactria and has goods from Shu—this shows it cannot be far from Shu.

sentences.zh: 今使大夏，從羌中，險，羌人惡之；

translations.literal: Now to send envoys to Da Xia by the Qiang route—dangerous; the Qiang hate it;
translations.idiomatic: To send envoys to Bactria now by the Qiang route is dangerous, and the Qiang dislike it;

sentences.zh: 少北，則為匈奴所得；

translations.literal: a little north and one is obtained by the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: a little to the north and one falls into Xiongnu hands;

sentences.zh: 從蜀，宜徑，又無寇。

translations.literal: from Shu—the route should be direct, and there are no raiders.
translations.idiomatic: from Shu the route should be direct, and there are no bandits.

sentences.zh: 天子既聞大宛及大夏、安息之屬皆大國，多奇物，土著，頗與中國同業，而兵弱，貴漢財物。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven having heard that Dayuan and Da Xia, Anxi and their kind are all great states, many rare goods, settle on the land, somewhat share China's industries, yet troops are weak and value Han wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had heard that Ferghana, Bactria, Parthia (Anxi), and their kind were all great states rich in rare goods, with settled populations and industries somewhat like China's, yet militarily weak and valuing Han wealth.

sentences.zh: 其北有大月氏、康居之屬，兵強，可以賂遺設利朝也。

translations.literal: To their north are the Greater Yuezhi, Kangju and their kind—troops strong; can be bribed and gifts sent to set up advantageous courts.
translations.idiomatic: To their north were the Greater Yuezhi, Kangju, and their kind—strong in arms and susceptible to bribes that could win favorable relations.

sentences.zh: 誠得而以義屬之，則廣地萬里，重九譯，致殊俗，威德遍於四海，欣然以騫言為然。

translations.literal: If sincerely obtained and by righteousness made subordinate, then land would extend ten thousand li, translation through nine interpreters, reaching alien customs, prestige and virtue throughout the four seas—he gladly took Qian's words as right.
translations.idiomatic: If they could truly be won and brought under righteous allegiance, territory would extend ten thousand li, messages would pass through nine interpreters to reach foreign peoples, and prestige would spread through the four seas—he gladly approved Zhang Qian's proposal.

sentences.zh: 乃令騫因蜀、犍為發間使-{王然于}-等四道並出：出駹，出冉，出徙，出邛、僰，指求身毒國，各行一二千里，其北方閉氐、莋，南方閉巂、昆明。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Qian through Shu and Jianwei to dispatch secret envoys including -{Wang Ranyu}- and others by four routes together: out from Qiang, out from Ran, out from Xi, out from Qiong and Bo—seeking Shendu; each traveled one or two thousand li; the north blocked by Di and Zhuo, the south blocked by Xi and Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zhang Qian, through Shu and Jianwei, to send secret envoys including Wang Ranyu and others by four routes at once: from Qiang, from Ran, from Xi, and from Qiong and Bo—all seeking India; each went one or two thousand li, but the north was blocked by the Di and Zhuo, and the south by Xi and Kunming.

sentences.zh: 昆明之屬無君長，善寇盜，輒殺略漢使，終莫得通。

translations.literal: The Kunming and their kind had no lord or chief, good at raiding and plundering—repeatedly killed and plundered Han envoys; in the end never got through.
translations.idiomatic: The Kunming and their kind had no rulers, were skilled at raiding, repeatedly killed and plundered Han envoys, and in the end the route never opened.

sentences.zh: 於是漢以求身毒道，始通滇國。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han in seeking the Shendu route first opened contact with the state of Dian.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, in seeking a route to India, Han first established contact with the state of Dian.

sentences.zh: 滇王當羌謂漢使者曰：「漢孰與我大？

translations.literal: The King of Dian, Dangqiang, said to Han's envoys: "Is Han as big as we are?
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dian, Dangqiang, said to the Han envoys, "Is Han as large as we are?

sentences.zh: 」及夜郎侯亦然。

translations.literal: " And the Marquis of Yelang was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: " And the Marquis of Yelang said the same.

sentences.zh: 以道不通，故各自以為一州主，不知漢廣大。

translations.literal: Because the road did not open, each therefore took himself as lord of a province, not knowing Han's vastness.
translations.idiomatic: Because the routes did not open, each thought himself the ruler of a whole province and did not know how vast Han was.

sentences.zh: 使者還，因盛言滇大國，足事親附；

translations.literal: The envoys returned and thereby spoke greatly of Dian as a great state, sufficient to serve with kinship and allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned, they spoke at length of Dian as a great state fit for kinship and allegiance;

sentences.zh: 天子注意焉，乃復事西南夷。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven took note and then again pursued affairs with the Southwest Yi.
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven took notice and again turned to affairs with the Southwest Yi.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，上幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor visited Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor visited Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: ----2三月，戊寅，平津獻侯公孫弘薨。

translations.literal: ----2 In the third month, on wuyin, Marquis Xian of Pingjin Gongsun Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the third month, on wuyin, Marquis Xian of Pingjin Gongsun Hong died.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以御史大夫樂安侯李蔡為丞相，廷尉張湯為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On renchen, Grand Counsellor Le'an Marquis Li Cai was made Chancellor, and Commandant of Justice Zhang Tang was made Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Grand Counsellor Le'an Marquis Li Cai was appointed Chancellor, and Commandant of Justice Zhang Tang was appointed Grand Counsellor.

sentences.zh: ----3霍去病為驃騎將軍，將萬騎出隴西，擊匈奴，歷五王國，轉戰六日，過焉支山千餘里，殺折蘭王，斬盧侯王，執渾邪王子及相國、都尉，獲首虜八千九百餘級，收休屠王祭天金人。

translations.literal: ----3 Huo Qubing was made General of Swift Cavalry, led ten thousand horsemen out from Longxi to strike the Xiongnu, passed through five kings' domains, fought turning for six days, crossed Yanzhi Mountain over a thousand li, killed King Zhelan, beheaded King Luhou, seized the son of King Hunye and the Chancellor and Commandant, obtained heads and captives eight thousand nine hundred odd, seized the Xiutu King's Golden Man for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Huo Qubing was made General of Swift Cavalry and led ten thousand horsemen out from Longxi to attack the Xiongnu; he passed through five kingdoms, fought for six days, and went more than a thousand li beyond Yanzhi Mountain; he killed King Zhelan, beheaded King Luhou, seized the son of King Hunye along with a chancellor and commandant, took eight thousand nine hundred-odd heads and captives, and captured the Xiutu King's golden image for sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 詔益封去病二千戶。

translations.literal: An edict increased Qubing's fief by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict increased Qubing's fief by two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 夏，去病復與合騎侯公孫敖將數萬騎俱出北地，異道。

translations.literal: In summer Qubing again with Marquis of Combined Cavalry Gongsun Ao led several tens of thousands of horsemen together out from Beidi by different routes.
