translations.idiomatic: In summer Qubing again led several tens of thousands of horsemen out from Beidi together with Marquis of Combined Cavalry Gongsun Ao, by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 衛尉張騫、郎中令李廣俱出右北平，異道。

translations.literal: Commandant of Guards Zhang Qian and Palace Attendant Li Guang both out from Right Beiping, different routes.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Guards Zhang Qian and Palace Attendant Li Guang both marched out from Right Beiping by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 廣將四千騎先行，可數百里，騫將萬騎在後。

translations.literal: Guang with four thousand horsemen went ahead perhaps several hundred li; Qian with ten thousand horsemen behind.
translations.idiomatic: Guang led four thousand horsemen ahead by several hundred li; Qian led ten thousand horsemen behind.

sentences.zh: 匈奴左賢王將四萬騎圍廣，廣軍士皆恐；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu Worthy King of the Left with forty thousand horsemen besieged Guang; Guang's soldiers were all afraid;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu Worthy King of the Left with forty thousand horsemen surrounded Guang; Guang's troops were all terrified;

sentences.zh: 廣乃使其子敢獨與數十騎馳貫胡騎，出其左右而還，告廣曰：「胡虜易與耳！

translations.literal: Guang then had his son Gan alone with several dozen horsemen gallop through Hu cavalry, exit their flanks and return, telling Guang: "The Hu bandits are easy to deal with!
translations.idiomatic: Guang then sent his son Gan alone with several dozen horsemen to charge through the Xiongnu cavalry, break out to their flanks, and return; he told Guang, "The Hu are easy to handle!

sentences.zh: 」軍士乃安。

translations.literal: " The soldiers then were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops were then reassured.

sentences.zh: 廣為圜陳，外向。

translations.literal: Guang formed a circular array facing outward.
translations.idiomatic: Guang formed a circular formation facing outward.

sentences.zh: 胡急擊之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The Hu pressed the attack; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu pressed the attack fiercely; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 漢兵死者過半，漢矢且盡。

translations.literal: Han soldiers dead over half; Han arrows nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the Han soldiers were dead, and their arrows were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 廣乃令士持滿毋發，而廣身自以大黃射其裨將，殺數人，胡虜益解。

translations.literal: Guang then ordered soldiers to hold full but not release; Guang himself with the great yellow bow shot their vice-general, killed several men; Hu bandits increasingly slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Guang then ordered his men to hold their bows drawn but not shoot; he himself used a powerful crossbow to shoot their vice-commander and killed several men, and the Xiongnu slackened their attack.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，吏士皆無人色，而廣意氣自如，益治軍，軍中皆服其勇。

translations.literal: At sunset officers and soldiers all had no complexion; yet Guang's spirit was as before, increasingly ordered the army; within the army all submitted to his courage.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset the officers and soldiers were ashen, yet Guang's bearing was calm as ever and he redoubled his command of the army; all in camp admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 明日，復力戰，死者過半，所殺亦過當。

translations.literal: Next day again fought fiercely; dead over half, those killed also exceeded the count.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again with all their strength; more than half died, but those they killed also exceeded their own losses.

sentences.zh: 會博望侯軍亦至，匈奴軍乃解去。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Expansive Vision's army also arrived, the Xiongnu army then dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Expansive Vision Zhang Qian's army also arrived, the Xiongnu force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢軍罷，弗能追，罷歸。

translations.literal: The Han army exhausted, could not pursue, withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Han army was exhausted and could not pursue; they withdrew and returned.

sentences.zh: 漢法：博望侯留遲後期，當死，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: Han law: Marquis of Expansive Vision detained late missing the rendezvous—death penalty, ransomed to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: By Han law, Marquis of Expansive Vision Zhang Qian, for arriving late, faced death but ransomed his life and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 廣軍功自如，無賞。

translations.literal: Guang's military achievement was as before, no reward.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's military achievement counted as even; he received no reward.

sentences.zh: 而驃騎將軍去病深入二千餘里，與合騎侯失，不相得。

translations.literal: Yet General of Swift Cavalry Qubing penetrated over two thousand li, missed Combined Cavalry Marquis, did not link up.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile General of Swift Cavalry Qubing penetrated more than two thousand li but missed Marquis of Combined Cavalry and failed to link up.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍逾居延，過小月氏，至祁連山，得單桓、酋塗王，及相國、都尉以眾降者二千五百人，斬首虜三萬二百級，獲裨小王七十餘人。

translations.literal: General of Swift Cavalry crossed Juyan, passed the Lesser Yuezhi, reached Qilian Mountains, obtained Kings Danhuan and Qiutu and Chancellor and Commandant with masses surrendering twenty-five hundred, beheaded captives thirty-two thousand, obtained over seventy vice-kings.
translations.idiomatic: General of Swift Cavalry Qubing crossed Juyan, passed the Lesser Yuezhi, and reached the Qilian Mountains; he took Kings Danhuan and Qiutu, along with a chancellor and commandant, with twenty-five hundred who surrendered; he beheaded thirty-two thousand and took more than seventy vice-kings.

sentences.zh: 天子益封去病五千戶，封其裨將有功者鷹擊司馬趙破奴為從驃侯，校尉高不識為宜冠侯，校尉僕多為煇渠侯。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven increased Qubing's fief five thousand households; enfeoffed his meritorious vice-generals—Hawk-strike Major Zhao Ponu as Follower Swift-Cavalry Marquis, Colonel Gao Bushi as Proper-Cap Marquis, Colonel Pudu as Huiqu Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven increased Qubing's fief by five thousand households and enfeoffed his meritorious subordinates: Hawk-strike Major Zhao Ponu as Follower Swift-Cavalry Marquis, Colonel Gao Bushi as Proper-Cap Marquis, and Colonel Pudu as Huiqu Marquis.

sentences.zh: 合騎侯敖坐行留不與驃騎會，當斬，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: Combined Cavalry Marquis Ao guilty of lingering march not meeting Swift Cavalry—decapitation, ransomed to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Combined Cavalry Gongsun Ao, for lingering and failing to join Swift Cavalry, faced decapitation but ransomed his life and became a commoner.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸宿將所將士、馬、兵皆不如驃騎，驃騎所將常選，然亦敢深入，常與壯騎先其大軍；

translations.literal: At this time veteran generals' soldiers, horses, arms were all inferior to Swift Cavalry; Swift Cavalry's troops were always picked, yet also dared deep penetration, often with elite cavalry ahead of the main army;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the soldiers, horses, and arms under the veteran generals were all inferior to Swift Cavalry's; Qubing's troops were always picked men, yet he also dared to penetrate deep, often riding ahead of the main army with elite horsemen;

sentences.zh: 軍亦有天幸，未嘗困絕也。

translations.literal: the army also had heaven's luck, never trapped to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: his army also enjoyed heaven's favor and was never trapped to the point of ruin.

sentences.zh: 而諸宿將常留落不偶，由此驃騎日以親貴，比大將軍矣。

translations.literal: Yet veteran generals often lagged behind without success; thereby Swift Cavalry daily grew intimate and honored, comparable to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: while the veteran generals often lagged behind without comparable success; thus Swift Cavalry grew daily more intimate and honored, rivaling the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 匈奴入代、雁門，殺略數百人。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu entered Dai and Yanmen, killed and plundered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu entered Dai and Yanmen and killed and plundered several hundred people.

sentences.zh: ----4江都王建與其父易王所幸淖姬等及女弟徵臣奸。

translations.literal: ----4 King Jian of Jiangdu committed incest with Nao Ji and others favored by his father King Yi, and his younger sister Zheng Chen.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 King Jian of Jiangdu committed incest with Nao Ji and others whom his father King Yi had favored, and with his younger sister Zheng Chen.

sentences.zh: 建游雷陂，天大風，建使郎二人乘小船入陂中。

translations.literal: Jian toured Lei Marsh; great wind; Jian sent two gentlemen-in-attendance in a small boat into the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Jian toured Lei Marsh during a great wind and sent two gentlemen-in-attendance in a small boat into the marsh.

sentences.zh: 船覆，兩郎溺，攀船，乍見乍沒。

translations.literal: The boat capsized; both drowned, clinging to the boat, now visible now submerged.
translations.idiomatic: The boat capsized; both men drowned, clinging to the boat and now appearing, now sinking from sight.

sentences.zh: 建臨觀大笑，令勿救，皆死。

translations.literal: Jian watched from shore laughing greatly, ordered no rescue—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Jian watched from the shore and laughed; he ordered that they not be rescued, and both died.

sentences.zh: 凡殺不辜三十五人，專為淫虐。

translations.literal: In all killed the innocent thirty-five persons, devoted to debauchery and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: In all he killed thirty-five innocents and devoted himself to debauchery and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 自知罪多，恐誅，與其-{后}-成光共使越婢下神，祝詛上。

translations.literal: Knowing his crimes were many, fearing execution, with his -{queen}- Chengguang together had a Yue slave-woman summon spirits, curse-prayed against the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his crimes were many and fearing execution, he and his queen Chengguang together had a Yue slave-woman summon spirits and curse the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又聞淮南、衡山陰謀，建亦作兵器，刻皇帝璽，為反具。

translations.literal: Also hearing Huainan and Hengshan secret plots, Jian also made weapons, carved the emperor's seal, prepared rebel equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Also hearing of the secret plots at Huainan and Hengshan, Jian made weapons, carved the emperor's seal, and prepared equipment for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事發覺，有司請捕誅，建自殺，-{后}-成光等皆棄市，國除。

translations.literal: Matters discovered; responsible offices requested arrest and execution—Jian killed himself, Chengguang and others all executed in market, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was discovered, the responsible offices requested arrest and execution; Jian killed himself, Chengguang and others were all executed in the market, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: ----5膠東康王寄薨。

translations.literal: ----5 King Kang of Jiaodong Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 King Kang of Jiaodong Ji died.

sentences.zh: ----6秋，匈奴渾邪王降。

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn the Xiongnu King Hunye surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn the Xiongnu King Hunye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是時，單于怒渾邪王、休屠王居西方為漢所殺虜數萬人，欲召誅之。

translations.literal: At this time the chanyu was angry that Kings Hunye and Xiutu dwelling in the west had tens of thousands killed and captured by Han, wished to summon and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the chanyu was angry that Kings Hunye and Xiutu in the west had had tens of thousands of their men killed and captured by Han and intended to summon and execute them.

sentences.zh: 渾邪王與休屠王恐，謀降漢，先遣使向邊境要遮漢人，令報天子。

translations.literal: Kings Hunye and Xiutu feared, plotted to surrender to Han, first sent envoys to the border to intercept Han men, ordering them to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Kings Hunye and Xiutu were afraid and plotted to surrender to Han; they first sent envoys to the border to intercept Han men and order them to report to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是時，大行李息將城河上，得渾邪王使，馳傳以聞。

translations.literal: At this time Grand Herald Li Xi was fortifying the river, obtained Hunye's envoy, relay-post hurried report.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Grand Herald Li Xi was fortifying the river and obtained Hunye's envoy; he sent a relay-post report.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之，恐其以詐降而襲邊，乃令驃騎將軍將兵往迎之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard, feared they might feign surrender to raid the border, then ordered Swift Cavalry General to lead troops to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven heard this, he feared they might feign surrender to raid the border and ordered General of Swift Cavalry to lead troops to receive them.

sentences.zh: 休屠王後悔，渾邪王殺之，并其眾。

translations.literal: Xiutu King repented; Hunye King killed him and merged their masses.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiutu repented, but King Hunye killed him and absorbed his followers.

sentences.zh: 驃騎既渡河，與渾邪王眾相望。

translations.literal: Swift Cavalry having crossed the river, faced Hunye King's masses from afar.
translations.idiomatic: After Swift Cavalry had crossed the river, he and King Hunye's forces faced each other from a distance.

sentences.zh: 渾邪王裨將見漢軍，而多不欲降者，頗遁去。

translations.literal: Hunye's vice-generals saw Han army, and many not wishing to surrender somewhat fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunye's vice-generals saw the Han army, many who did not wish to surrender fled in considerable numbers.

sentences.zh: 驃騎乃馳入，得與渾邪王相見，斬其欲亡者八千人，遂獨遣渾邪王乘傳詣至行在所，盡將其眾渡河。

translations.literal: Swift Cavalry then galloped in, met Hunye King, beheaded eight thousand who wished to flee, then alone sent Hunye King by relay carriage to reach the imperial traveling residence, entirely led their masses across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Swift Cavalry then galloped in, met King Hunye, and beheaded eight thousand who wished to flee; he then sent King Hunye alone by relay carriage to the emperor's traveling residence and led all his followers across the river.

sentences.zh: 降者四萬餘人，號稱十萬。

translations.literal: Surrenderers forty-odd thousand, claimed as one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The surrenderers numbered more than forty thousand, though they claimed one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 既至長安，天子所以賞賜者數十巨萬；

translations.literal: Having reached Chang'an, what the Son of Heaven bestowed in rewards was several tens of millions;
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached Chang'an, the Son of Heaven's rewards amounted to several tens of millions;

sentences.zh: 封渾邪王萬戶，為漯陰侯，封其裨王呼毒尼等四人皆為列侯。

translations.literal: enfeoffed Hunye King ten thousand households as Marquis of Luoyin, enfeoffed his vice-kings Huduni and four others all as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed King Hunye with ten thousand households as Marquis of Luoyin and enfeoffed his vice-kings Huduni and four others as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 益封驃騎千七百戶。

translations.literal: Increased Swift Cavalry's fief seventeen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He increased Swift Cavalry's fief by seventeen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 渾邪之降也，漢發車二萬乘以迎之，縣官無錢，從民貰馬，民或匿馬，馬不具。

translations.literal: At Hunye's surrender Han dispatched twenty thousand carriages to welcome; the government had no money, borrowed horses from the people; people hid horses—horses not complete.
translations.idiomatic: At Hunye's surrender Han dispatched twenty thousand carriages to receive him; the government had no money and borrowed horses from the people, but some people hid their horses and the horses were not sufficient.

sentences.zh: 上怒，欲斬長安令，右內史汲黯曰：「長安令無罪，獨斬臣黯，民乃肯出馬。

translations.literal: The emperor angry, wished to behead the Magistrate of Chang'an; Right Metropolitan Superintendent Ji An said: "The Magistrate of Chang'an is without guilt; only behead your servant Ji An, then the people would be willing to lend horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and wished to behead the Magistrate of Chang'an; Right Metropolitan Superintendent Ji An said, "The Magistrate of Chang'an is guiltless; only behead your servant Ji An, and then the people will be willing to lend horses.

sentences.zh: 且匈奴畔其主而降漢，漢徐以縣次傳之，何至令天下騷動，罷敝中國而以事夷狄之人乎！

translations.literal: Moreover the Xiongnu turned against their lord and surrendered to Han—Han should leisurely pass them by county stages for relay; why reach the point of stirring all under Heaven, exhausting China to serve barbarian men!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Xiongnu turned against their lord and surrendered to Han; Han should convey them leisurely by relay stages from county to county—why stir all under Heaven to exhaustion and wear out China to serve barbarian men!

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 及渾邪至，賈人與市者坐當死五百餘人，黯請間見高門，曰：「夫匈奴攻當路塞，絕和親，中國興兵誅之，死傷者不可勝計，而費以巨萬百數。

translations.literal: When Hunye arrived, merchants who traded with them guilty facing death over five hundred; Ji An requested private audience at Gaomen Gate, saying: "The Xiongnu attacked the passes on the road, severed marriage alliance; China raised troops to punish—dead and wounded beyond counting, costs in hundreds of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunye arrived, more than five hundred merchants who had traded with them faced death; Ji An requested a private audience at Gaomen Gate and said, "The Xiongnu attacked the frontier passes, severed the marriage alliance, and China raised troops to punish them; the dead and wounded are beyond counting, and the cost runs to hundreds of tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為陛下得胡人，皆以為奴婢，以賜從軍死事者家，所鹵獲，因予之，以謝天下之苦，塞百姓之心。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks when Your Majesty obtains Hu men, all should be made slaves and maidservants, given to families of those who followed the army and died in service; booty seized thereby given them—to thank all under Heaven's suffering, stop the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant foolishly thinks that whatever Hu captives Your Majesty obtains should all be made slaves and maidservants and given to the families of men who followed the army and died in service, and whatever booty is seized should be given them as well—to repay the suffering of all under Heaven and satisfy the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 今縱不能，渾邪率數萬之眾來降，虛府庫賞賜，發良民侍養，譬若奉驕子，愚民安知市買長安中物，而文吏繩以為闌出財物於邊關乎！

translations.literal: Now even if not possible—Hunye leading tens of thousands come to surrender, emptying the treasury in rewards, sending good people to attend and nourish, like tending a spoiled child—foolish people how know to buy things in Chang'an, yet clerk officials bind them as sneaking goods out past the border pass!
translations.idiomatic: Now even if that cannot be done, Hunye has led tens of thousands to surrender, emptying the treasury in rewards and sending good citizens to attend them, as if tending a spoiled child; how would foolish people know how to buy goods in Chang'an, yet clerk officials bind them for smuggling property out past the border pass!

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不能得匈奴之資以謝天下，又以微文殺無知者五百餘人，是所謂庇其葉而傷其枝者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty even if unable to obtain Xiongnu assets to thank all under Heaven, yet with petty documents kill ignorant over five hundred—this is what is called sheltering the leaves and harming the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, even if unable to use Xiongnu wealth to repay all under Heaven, yet kills more than five hundred ignorant men on petty legal grounds—this is what is called sheltering the leaves while harming the branches.

sentences.zh: 臣竊為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers Your Majesty should not take this.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately considers that Your Majesty should not do this.

sentences.zh: 」上默然不許，曰：「吾久不聞汲黯之言，今又復妄發矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor silent, not granting, said: "I have long not heard Ji An's words; now again he rashly speaks.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was silent and did not grant his request, saying, "I have long not heard Ji An's words; now again he speaks rashly.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，乃分徙降者邊五郡故塞外，而皆在河南，因其故俗為五屬國。

translations.literal: Before long, then divided and relocated the surrenderers to the five border commanderies' old lands outside the passes—all south of the river—according to their former customs making five dependent states.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they divided and relocated the surrenderers to the old lands outside the passes in the five border commanderies—all south of the Yellow River—and, according to their former customs, established five dependent states.

sentences.zh: 而金城河西，西並南山至鹽澤，空無匈奴，匈奴時有候者到而希矣。

translations.literal: And west of Jincheng and Hexi, west along the southern mountains to Salt Marsh, empty of Xiongnu; when Xiongnu scouts sometimes came they were few.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jincheng and Hexi, west along the southern mountains to Salt Marsh, the land was empty of Xiongnu; when Xiongnu scouts occasionally came, they were few.

sentences.zh: 休屠王太子日磾與母閼氏、弟倫俱沒入官，輸黃門養馬。

translations.literal: Xiutu King's crown prince Rizi and mother the chanyu's wife and brother Lun all confiscated to government, sent to Yellow Gate to raise horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiutu King's crown prince Rizi, his mother the chanyu's wife, and his brother Lun were all confiscated by the government and sent to the Yellow Gate to raise horses.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝游宴，見馬，後宮滿側，日磾等數十人牽馬過殿下，莫不竊視，至日磾獨不敢。

translations.literal: Long after, the emperor at feast saw horses; inner palace filled the sides; Rizi and several dozen leading horses past the hall steps—all stole glances; when it reached Rizi alone he dared not.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, at an imperial feast the emperor saw horses; the inner palace filled both sides; Rizi and several dozen others led horses past the hall steps—all stole glances, but when it came to Rizi alone he did not dare.

sentences.zh: 日磾長八尺二寸，容貌甚嚴，馬又肥好，上異而問之，具以本狀對。

translations.literal: Rizi eight chi two cun tall, appearance very stern, horses also fat and fine—the emperor found it strange and asked; fully reported his original condition.
translations.idiomatic: Rizi was eight chi two cun tall, of very stern appearance, and the horses were fat and fine; the emperor found it strange and asked him; he fully reported his origins.

sentences.zh: 對奇焉，即日賜湯沐、衣冠，拜為馬監，遷侍中、駙馬都尉、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Answering strangely pleased him; that very day bestowed bath funds, cap and robes; appointed Horse Supervisor; promoted Palace Attendant, Commandant of Chariots for the Empress's Carriages, Household Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was strangely pleased with his answer; that very day he bestowed bath funds, cap, and robes, appointed him Horse Supervisor, and promoted him to Palace Attendant, Commandant of Chariots for the Empress's Carriages, and Household Counsellor.

sentences.zh: 日磾既親近，未嘗有過失，上甚信愛之，賞賜累千金，出則驂乘，入侍左右。

translations.literal: Rizi once intimate, never had fault—the emperor greatly trusted and loved him; rewards accumulated thousands in gold; going out rode alongside chariot, entering served left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rizi was close at hand he never had a fault; the emperor greatly trusted and loved him, bestowed rewards totaling thousands in gold, had him ride alongside when going out, and attend at his left and right when entering.

sentences.zh: 貴戚多竊怨曰：「陛下妄得一胡兒，反貴重之。

translations.literal: Noble kin mostly secretly complained: "Your Majesty randomly obtained a Hu child, yet instead honors him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Many among the noble kin secretly complained, "Your Majesty randomly obtained a Hu child, yet instead honors him heavily.

sentences.zh: 」上聞，愈厚焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor heard, all the more treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard this, he treated him all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 以休屠作金人為祭天主，故賜日磾姓金氏。

translations.literal: Because Xiutu made a golden man as sacrifice lord of Heaven, therefore gave Rizi the surname Jin (Gold).
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiutu had made a golden man as lord of Heaven for sacrifice, he gave Rizi the surname Jin (Gold).

sentences.zh: 1春，有星孛於東方。

translations.literal: 1 In spring a broom star cometed in the east.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring a broom star appeared in the east.

translations.literal: ----2 Summer, fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: Amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: There was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----3淮南王之謀反也，膠東康王寄微聞其事，私作戰守備。

translations.literal: ----3 At the King of Huainan's plotting rebellion, King Kang of Jiaodong Ji faintly heard the matter, privately made battle and defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 When the King of Huainan plotted rebellion, King Kang of Jiaodong Ji faintly heard of it and privately made preparations for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 及吏治淮南事，辭出之。

translations.literal: When officials tried the Huainan case, testimony brought it out.
translations.idiomatic: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, testimony brought it to light.

sentences.zh: 寄母王夫人，即皇太后之女弟也，於上最親，意自傷，發病而死，不敢置後。

translations.literal: Ji's mother Lady Wang—that is the Empress Dowager's younger sister—most intimate with the emperor; she herself grieved, fell ill and died, dared not arrange a successor.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's mother Lady Wang was the Empress Dowager's younger sister and was closest to the emperor; grieving on her own account, she fell ill and died and dared not arrange a successor.

sentences.zh: 上聞而憐之，立其長子賢為膠東王。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and pitied, established eldest son Xian as King of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he pitied them and established the eldest son Xian as King of Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 又封其所愛少子慶為六安王，王故衡山王地。

translations.literal: Also enfeoffed beloved younger son Qing as King of Lu'an, ruling the former King of Hengshan's lands.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed the beloved younger son Qing as King of Lu'an, granting him the former lands of the King of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: ----4秋，匈奴入右北平、定襄，各數萬騎，殺略千餘人。

translations.literal: ----4 In autumn Xiongnu entered Right Beiping and Dingxiang—each several ten thousand horsemen—killed and plundered over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In autumn the Xiongnu entered Right Beiping and Dingxiang with several ten thousand horsemen each and killed and plundered more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: ----5山東大水，民多饑乏。

translations.literal: ----5 In the lands east of the passes there was great flooding; among the people many were hungry and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the lands east of the passes there was great flooding, and many among the people were hungry and destitute.

sentences.zh: 天子遣使者虛郡國倉癐以振貧民，猶不足，又募豪富吏民能假貸貧民者以名聞，尚不能相救。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent envoys to empty the commanderies' and kingdoms' granaries to relieve the poor people; still it was insufficient; moreover he recruited powerful and wealthy officials and commoners who could lend to the poor to have their names reported—yet they still could not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to empty the commanderies' and kingdoms' granaries to relieve the poor; still it was not enough, and he recruited wealthy officials and commoners who could lend to the poor to have their names reported—yet they still could not rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 乃徙貧民於關以西及充朔方以南新秦中七十餘萬口，衣食皆仰給縣官，數歲假予產業。

translations.literal: Thereupon the poor people were moved west of the pass and to fill the new Qin territory south of Shuofang—more than seven hundred thousand mouths; food and clothing all looked up to be supplied by the county officials; for several years they were lent and given property.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon more than seven hundred thousand poor people were moved west of the pass and settled in the new Qin territory south of Shuofang; food and clothing were all supplied by the government, and for several years they were lent land and property.

sentences.zh: 使者分部護之，冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: Envoys were divided into sections to guard them; official hats and canopies gazed at one another.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were assigned in districts to escort them, with official canopies and banners in sight everywhere.

sentences.zh: 其費以億計，不可勝數。

translations.literal: The expense was reckoned in hundreds of millions and could not be completely counted.
translations.idiomatic: The expense ran to hundreds of millions and could not be reckoned.

sentences.zh: ----6漢既得渾邪王地，隴西、北地、上郡益少胡寇，詔減三郡戍卒之半，以寬天下之繇。

translations.literal: ----6 Han having already obtained the lands of King Hunye, Longxi, Beidi, and Shang commandery increasingly had fewer Hu raiders; an edict reduced the garrison soldiers of the three commanderies by half, to ease all under Heaven's corvée.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Once Han had taken the lands of King Hunye, Longxi, Beidi, and Shang commandery saw fewer Xiongnu raids; an edict cut the garrison troops of the three commanderies by half to ease corvée labor throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: ----7上將討昆明，以昆明有滇池方三百里，乃作昆明池以習水戰。

translations.literal: ----7 The emperor was about to attack Kunming; because Kunming had Dian Lake, a square of three hundred li, he therefore made Kunming Pool to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 The emperor planned to attack Kunming; because Kunming had Dian Lake, some three hundred li square, he built Kunming Pool to practice naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 是時法既益嚴，吏多廢免。

translations.literal: At this time the laws had already grown stricter; many officials were dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the laws had grown stricter, and many officials were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 兵革數動，民多買復及五大夫，征發之士益鮮。

translations.literal: Arms and armor moved several times; the people mostly bought exemption and the rank of grand master of five; conscripted soldiers grew increasingly few.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were frequent; many people bought exemption from service and the rank of grand master of five, and conscripts grew ever scarcer.

sentences.zh: 於是除千夫、五大夫為吏，不欲者出馬，以故吏弄法，皆謫令伐棘上林，穿昆明池。

translations.literal: Thereupon thousand-leaders and grand masters of five were exempted to serve as officials; those unwilling gave horses; because former officials twisted the law, all were banished and ordered to cut thorns in Shanglin and dig through to Kunming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon thousand-leaders and grand masters of five were made officials; those unwilling provided horses instead; and because former officials twisted the law, all were banished to cut thorns in Shanglin and excavate Kunming Pool.

sentences.zh: ----8是歲，得神馬於渥窪水中。

translations.literal: ----8 This year, a divine horse was obtained in the Wowa waters.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 This year a divine horse was obtained in the Wowa waters.

sentences.zh: 上方立樂府，使司馬相如等造為詩賦，以宦者李延年為協律都尉，佩二千石印；

translations.literal: Above, the Music Bureau was established; Sima Xiangru and others were made to compose poems and rhapsodies; the eunuch Li Yanian was made Director of Harmonizing the Pitch Pipes, wearing a two-thousand-bushel seal;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor established the Music Bureau, had Sima Xiangru and others compose poems and rhapsodies, and made the eunuch Li Yanian Director of Harmonizing the Pitch Pipes, with a two-thousand-bushel seal;

sentences.zh: 弦次初詩以合八音之調。

translations.literal: Strings arranged the newly composed poems to match the tones of the eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: string instruments set the new poems to the modes of the eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 詩多《爾雅》之文，通一經之士不能獨知其辭，必集會《五經》家相與共講習讀之，乃能通知其意。

translations.literal: The poems mostly had the language of the Erya; a scholar who had mastered one classic could not alone know their wording—they had to gather and meet with masters of the Five Classics to study and read them together, and only then could they fully know their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The poems mostly used the language of the Erya; even a scholar who had mastered one classic could not know their wording alone—they had to gather masters of the Five Classics to study and read them together before they could fully grasp their meaning.

sentences.zh: 及得神馬，次以為歌。

translations.literal: When the divine horse was obtained, it was next made into a song.
translations.idiomatic: When the divine horse was obtained, it was next set as a song.

sentences.zh: 汲黯曰：「凡王者作樂，上以承祖宗，下以化兆民。

translations.literal: Ji An said: "In general when kings make music, above it carries on the ancestors, below it transforms the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An said, "In general when kings make music, above it carries on the ancestors, below it transforms the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 今陛下得馬，詩以為歌，協於宗廟，先帝百姓豈能知其音邪？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty obtained a horse and made a poem into a song to harmonize in the ancestral temple—can the former emperor's hundred surnames know its sound?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has obtained a horse and made a poem into a song for the ancestral temple—can the former emperor's common people know its sound?

sentences.zh: 」上默然不說。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent and not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was silent and displeased.

sentences.zh: 上招延士大夫，常如不足；

translations.literal: The emperor recruited and extended welcome to scholar-officials, always as if they were insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recruited scholar-officials, always as if there were never enough;

sentences.zh: 然性嚴峻，群臣雖素所愛信者，或小有犯法，或欺罔，輒按誅之，無所寬假。

translations.literal: yet his nature was stern and severe; among the ministers, even those he had long loved and trusted—if they slightly violated the law or deceived—he would immediately investigate and execute them, with no lenience.
translations.idiomatic: yet his nature was stern; among the ministers, even those he had long loved and trusted—if they slightly broke the law or deceived—he would immediately investigate and execute them without lenience.

sentences.zh: 汲黯諫曰：「陛下求賢甚勞，未盡其用，輒已殺之。

translations.literal: Ji An remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty seeks the worthy with great toil, yet before their use is exhausted you have already killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty seeks the worthy with great toil, yet before their use is exhausted you have already killed them.

sentences.zh: 以有限之士恣無已之誅，臣恐天下賢才將盡，陛下誰與共為治乎！

translations.literal: With a limited supply of scholars you indulge unending executions—your servant fears the realm's worthy talents will be exhausted; with whom will Your Majesty together govern?
translations.idiomatic: With a limited supply of men you indulge unending executions—your servant fears the realm's worthy talents will be exhausted; with whom will Your Majesty govern?

sentences.zh: 」黯言之甚怒，上笑而諭之曰：「何世無才，患人不能識之耳，苟能識之，何患無人！

translations.literal: " Ji An spoke very angrily; the emperor smiled and instructed him, saying: "What age lacks talent? The affliction is only that men cannot recognize it; if one can recognize it, why fear there will be no men!
translations.idiomatic: " Ji An spoke in great anger; the emperor smiled and instructed him, saying, "What age lacks talent? The trouble is only that men cannot recognize it; if one can recognize it, why fear there will be no men!

sentences.zh: 夫所謂才者，猶有用之器也，有才而不肯盡用，與無才同，不殺何施！

translations.literal: What is called talent is like a vessel with a use; having talent yet unwilling to exhaust its use is the same as having no talent—if you do not kill them, what is the use!
translations.idiomatic: What is called talent is like a vessel with a use; having talent yet unwilling to use it fully is the same as having no talent—if you do not kill them, what is the use!

sentences.zh: 」黯曰：「臣雖不能以言屈陛下，而心猶以為非。

translations.literal: " Ji An said: "Your servant, though unable by words to bend Your Majesty, in heart still thinks it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji An said, "Your servant, though unable by words to bend Your Majesty, in heart still thinks it wrong.

sentences.zh: 願陛下自今改之，無以臣為愚而不知理也。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty from now to change this and not take your servant as foolish and ignorant of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty from now to change this and not take your servant for a fool who knows nothing of principle.

sentences.zh: 」上顧群臣曰：「黯自言為便辟則不可，自言為愚，豈不信然乎！

translations.literal: " The emperor looked at the ministers and said: "If Ji An calls himself a fawning partisan, that will not do; if he calls himself foolish, is that not truly so!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor looked at the ministers and said, "If Ji An calls himself a fawning partisan, that will not do; if he calls himself a fool, is that not truly so!

sentences.zh: 1冬，有司言：「縣官用度太空，而富商大賈冶鑄、煮鹽，財或累萬金，不佐國家之急。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the responsible officials said: "The county officials' expenditures are greatly empty, yet great wealthy merchants smelt, cast, and boil salt; wealth sometimes accumulates to tens of thousands in gold, yet they do not assist the state's urgency.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the responsible officials said, "Government expenditures are greatly depleted, yet great wealthy merchants smelt, cast, and boil salt; wealth sometimes piles to tens of thousands in gold, yet they do not assist the state's urgent needs.

sentences.zh: 請更錢造幣以贍用，而摧浮淫并兼之徒。

translations.literal: We request to remint money and make currency to supply use, and to crush those who float in excess and merge by annexation.
translations.idiomatic: We request to remint currency to supply expenditures and to crush those who grow fat on extravagance and monopoly.

sentences.zh: 」是時，禁苑有白鹿而少府多銀、錫，乃以白鹿皮方尺，緣以藻繢，為皮幣，直四十萬。

translations.literal: " At this time the forbidden park had a white deer and the Privy Treasury had much silver and tin; thereupon a square foot of white deer skin, edged with embroidered ornament, was made into leather currency worth four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time the imperial park had a white deer and the Privy Treasury had much silver and tin; they took a square foot of white deer skin, edged it with embroidered ornament, and made leather currency worth four hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 王侯、宗室，朝覲、聘享，必以皮幣薦璧，然後得行。

translations.literal: Kings, marquises, and the imperial clan, for court audiences and presentation offerings, had to present jade bi with leather currency and only then could proceed.
translations.idiomatic: When kings, marquises, and the imperial clan attended court or made offerings, they had to present jade bi with leather currency and only then could proceed.

sentences.zh: 又造銀、錫為白金三品：大者圜之，其文龍，直三千；

translations.literal: Moreover silver and tin were made into white metal in three grades: the large was made round, its inscription a dragon, worth three thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they made silver and tin into white metal in three grades: the large was made round, inscribed with a dragon, worth three thousand;

sentences.zh: 次方之，其文馬，直五百；

translations.literal: the next was made square, its inscription a horse, worth five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: the next was made square, inscribed with a horse, worth five hundred;

sentences.zh: 小者橢之，其文龜，直三百。

translations.literal: the small was made oval, its inscription a turtle, worth three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: the small was made oval, inscribed with a turtle, worth three hundred.

sentences.zh: 令縣官銷半兩錢，更鑄三銖錢，盜鑄諸金錢罪皆死；

translations.literal: It was ordered that the county officials melt down banliang coins and remint three-zhu coins; stealing cast of all metal currency—crime all death;
translations.idiomatic: The government was ordered to melt down banliang coins and remint three-zhu coins; counterfeiting any metal currency was punishable by death;

sentences.zh: 而吏民之盜鑄白金者不可勝數。

translations.literal: yet among officials and people those who stole cast white metal could not be completely counted.
translations.idiomatic: yet among officials and people those who counterfeited white metal could not be counted.

sentences.zh: 於是以東郭咸陽、孔僅為大農丞，領鹽鐵事；

translations.literal: Thereupon Dongguo Xianyang and Kong Jin were made aides to the Grand Farmer, overseeing salt and iron affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Dongguo Xianyang and Kong Jin were made aides to the Grand Farmer to oversee salt and iron;

sentences.zh: 桑弘羊以計算用事。

translations.literal: Sang Hongyang by reckoning and calculation handled affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Hongyang handled affairs through reckoning and calculation.

sentences.zh: 咸陽，齊之大煮鹽；

translations.literal: Xianyang was Qi's great salt-boiler;
translations.idiomatic: Xianyang was Qi's great salt-boiler;

sentences.zh: 僅，南陽大冶，皆致生累千金。

translations.literal: Jin of Nanyang was a great smelter; both brought forth livelihood accumulating a thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Jin of Nanyang was a great smelter; both had amassed wealth of a thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 弘羊，洛陽賈人之子，以心計，年十三侍中。

translations.literal: Hongyang was a Luoyang merchant's son; by mental calculation, at age thirteen he became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyang was a Luoyang merchant's son; by mental calculation, at age thirteen he became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三人言利，事析秋毫矣。

translations.literal: The three men spoke of profit; affairs were analyzed down to an autumn down.
translations.idiomatic: The three men spoke of profit and analyzed affairs down to the finest hair.

sentences.zh: 詔禁民敢私鑄鐵器、煮鹽者釱左趾，沒入其器物。

translations.literal: An edict forbade the people to dare privately cast iron tools or boil salt—such ones were branded on the left toe with iron, and their tools were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade the people to dare privately cast iron tools or boil salt—offenders were branded on the left toe and their goods confiscated.

sentences.zh: 公卿又請令諸賈人末作各以其物自占，率緡錢二千而一算；

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers further requested to order all merchants and downstream craftsmen each to report their goods themselves, levying two thousand cash in stringed money per calculation unit;
translations.idiomatic: The dukes and ministers further requested that all merchants and craftsmen report their goods themselves, with a levy of two thousand cash per calculation unit;

sentences.zh: 及民有軺車若船五丈以上者，皆有算。

translations.literal: and for the people who had light carriages or boats of more than five zhang, all had levies.
translations.idiomatic: and for people who owned light carriages or boats of more than five zhang, levies applied as well.

sentences.zh: 匿不自占，占不悉，戍邊一歲，沒入緡錢。

translations.literal: Those who concealed and did not report themselves, or reported incompletely, were garrisoned on the border one year and their stringed money was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Those who concealed goods and did not report, or reported incompletely, were garrisoned on the border for one year and their cash was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 有能告者，以其半畀之。

translations.literal: Those able to inform had half given to them.
translations.idiomatic: Informers received half the confiscated sum.

sentences.zh: 其法大抵出張湯。

translations.literal: The law mostly came from Zhang Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The law mostly came from Zhang Tang.

sentences.zh: 湯每朝奏事，語國家用，日晏，天子忘食。

translations.literal: Whenever Tang presented affairs at court and spoke of state expenditures, the day grew late and the Son of Heaven forgot his meal.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tang presented affairs at court and spoke of state expenditures, the day grew late and the emperor forgot his meal.

sentences.zh: 丞相充位，天下事皆決於湯。

translations.literal: The chancellor filled the post in name; affairs of all under Heaven were all decided by Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor filled the post in name; affairs of all under Heaven were all decided by Tang.

sentences.zh: 百姓騷動，不安其生，咸指怨湯。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames were disturbed and unsettled in their livelihoods; all pointed and blamed Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The people were disturbed and unsettled in their livelihoods; all blamed Tang.

sentences.zh: ----2初，河南人卜式，數請輸財縣官以助邊，天子使使問式：「欲官乎？

translations.literal: ----2 Initially, Bu Shi of Henan several times requested to transport wealth to the county officials to assist the border; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy to ask Shi: "Do you wish an office?
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Initially Bu Shi of Henan several times offered to give wealth to the government to assist the border; the emperor sent an envoy to ask Shi, "Do you wish an office?

sentences.zh: 」式曰：「臣少田牧，不習仕宦，不願也。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "Your servant from youth farmed and herded; I am not practiced in office and service—I do not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "Your servant from youth has farmed and herded; I am not practiced in office and do not wish it.

sentences.zh: 」使者問曰：「家豈有冤，欲言事乎？

translations.literal: " The envoy asked: "Does your family perhaps have a grievance and you wish to speak of the matter?
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy asked, "Does your family perhaps have a grievance you wish to report?

sentences.zh: 」式曰：「臣生與人無分爭，邑人貧者貸之，不善者教之，所居人皆從式，式何故見冤於人！

translations.literal: " Shi said: "Your servant in life has had no quarrels with others; when townsmen were poor I lent to them, when they were unskilled I taught them—where I have lived, people all followed Shi; why should Shi be wronged by others!
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "Your servant has had no quarrels with others in life; when townsmen were poor I lent to them, when they were unskilled I taught them—where I have lived, people all followed Shi; why should Shi be wronged by anyone!

sentences.zh: 無所欲言也。

translations.literal: There is nothing I wish to say.
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing I wish to say.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「苟如此，子何欲而然？

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "If it is so, why do you wish to do this?
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said, "If it is so, why do you wish to do this?

sentences.zh: 」式曰：「天子誅匈奴，愚以為賢者宜死節於邊，有財者宜輸委，如此而匈奴可滅也。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "The Son of Heaven punishes the Xiongnu; your servant thinks the worthy ought to die holding the border, the wealthy ought to transport and surrender their goods—thus the Xiongnu can be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "The emperor punishes the Xiongnu; your servant thinks the worthy ought to die holding the border and the wealthy ought to surrender their goods—thus the Xiongnu can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」上由是賢之，欲尊顯以風百姓，乃召拜式為中郎，爵左庶長，賜田十頃，佈告下天，使明知之。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereby considered him worthy, wished to honor and display him to instruct the hundred surnames, and thereupon summoned and appointed Shi as Palace Attendant, ennobling him as left commoner chief, granting ten qing of fields, proclaiming it below Heaven so all clearly knew.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereby considered him worthy and wished to honor him to instruct the people; he summoned and appointed Shi as Palace Attendant, granted him the rank of left commoner chief and ten qing of fields, and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又擢式為齊太傅。

translations.literal: Before long, Shi was further promoted to Grand Tutor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Shi was further promoted to Grand Tutor of Qi.

sentences.zh: ----3春，有星孛於東北。

translations.literal: ----3 In spring, a broom star appeared in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring, a comet appeared in the northeast.

sentences.zh: 夏，有長星出於西北。

translations.literal: In summer, a long star appeared in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, a long comet appeared in the northwest.

sentences.zh: ----4上與諸將議曰：「翕侯趙信為單于畫計，常以為漢兵不能度幕輕留，今大發士卒，其勢必得所欲。

translations.literal: ----4 The emperor deliberated with the generals, saying: "Marquis of Xi Zhao Xin made plans for the chanyu, always thinking Han troops cannot cross the desert screen and stay lightly; now with a great dispatch of soldiers, their momentum is certain to obtain what they desire.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The emperor deliberated with the generals, saying, "Marquis of Xi Zhao Xin advised the chanyu, always thinking Han troops cannot cross the desert and linger lightly; now with a great dispatch of troops, their momentum is certain to obtain what they desire.

sentences.zh: 」乃粟馬十萬，令大將軍青、驃騎將軍去病各將五萬騎，私負從馬復四萬匹，步兵轉者踵軍後又數十萬人，而敢力戰深入之士皆屬驃騎。

translations.literal: " Thereupon grain-fed horses numbered a hundred thousand; the Great General Qing and the Swift Cavalry General Huo Qubing were each ordered to lead fifty thousand horsemen, with privately carried follower horses adding forty thousand more; infantry transport troops following the army's rear numbered several hundred thousand more; and the men who dared fight fiercely and penetrate deep all belonged to the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon a hundred thousand grain-fed horses were gathered; the Great General Wei Qing and Swift Cavalry General Huo Qubing were each to lead fifty thousand horsemen, with privately carried follower horses adding forty thousand more; infantry transport troops following the rear numbered several hundred thousand more; and the men who dared fight fiercely and penetrate deep all belonged to Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 驃騎始為出定襄，當單于，捕虜言單于東，乃更令驃騎出代郡，令大將軍出定襄。

translations.literal: The Swift Cavalry at first was to go out from Dingxiang to meet the chanyu; captives said the chanyu was east, so the order was changed: the Swift Cavalry was to go out from Dai commandery and the Great General from Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Qubing was at first to go out from Dingxiang to meet the chanyu; captives said the chanyu was to the east, so the order was changed: Huo Qubing was to go out from Dai commandery and the Great General from Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 郎中令李廣數自請行，天子以為老，弗許；

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Guang several times himself requested to go on campaign; the Son of Heaven thought him old and did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Li Guang several times requested to go on campaign; the emperor thought him old and did not permit it;

sentences.zh: 良久，乃許之，以為前將軍。

translations.literal: after a long while he then permitted it and made him Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: after a long while he permitted it and made him Forward General.

sentences.zh: 太僕公孫賀為左將軍，主爵都尉趙食其為右將軍，平陽侯曹瓤為後將軍，皆屬大將軍。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He was made Left General, Chief Commandant of Nobility Zhao Shiyi was made Right General, Marquis of Pingyang Cao Rang was made Rear General—all subordinate to the Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Stud Gongsun He was made Left General, Chief Commandant of Nobility Zhao Shiyi Right General, and Marquis of Pingyang Cao Rang Rear General—all subordinate to the Great General.

sentences.zh: 趙信為單于謀曰：「漢兵既度幕，人馬罷，匈奴可坐收虜耳。

translations.literal: Zhao Xin advised the chanyu, saying: "Han troops having already crossed the desert screen, men and horses are exhausted—the Xiongnu can sit and take the captives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin advised the chanyu, saying, "Once Han troops have crossed the desert, men and horses will be exhausted—the Xiongnu can sit and take the captives.

sentences.zh: 」乃悉遠北其輜重，以精兵待幕北。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they moved all baggage far north and waited north of the desert screen with picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they moved all baggage far north and waited north of the desert with picked troops.

sentences.zh: 大將軍青既出塞，捕虜知單于所居，乃自以精兵走之，而令前將軍廣并於右將軍軍，出東道。

translations.literal: The Great General Qing having gone out beyond the frontier, captives knew where the chanyu dwelt; he thereupon himself with picked troops hurried there, and ordered Forward General Guang merged into the Right General's army to go out by the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: The Great General Wei Qing having gone out beyond the frontier, captives knew where the chanyu dwelt; he himself hurried there with picked troops and ordered Forward General Li Guang merged into the Right General's army to go out by the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 東道回遠而水草少，廣自請曰：「臣部為前將軍，今大將軍乃徙令臣出東道。

translations.literal: The eastern route was circuitous and far, with little water and grass; Guang himself requested, saying: "Your servant's division was the Forward General; now the Great General has moved and ordered your servant out by the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern route was circuitous and far, with little water and grass; Guang himself requested, saying, "Your servant's command was Forward General; now the Great General has moved and ordered your servant out by the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 且臣結髮而與匈奴戰，今乃一得當單于，臣願居前，先死單于。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant from tying up hair has fought the Xiongnu; now at last I may meet the chanyu—your servant wishes to stand forward and be first to die facing the chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your servant has fought the Xiongnu since boyhood; now at last I may meet the chanyu—your servant wishes to stand forward and face the chanyu first.

sentences.zh: 」大將軍亦陰受上誡，以為「李廣老，數奇，毋令當單于，恐不得所欲。

translations.literal: " The Great General had also secretly received the emperor's warning, thinking: "Li Guang is old and his fate is odd—do not let him meet the chanyu, lest he fail to obtain what is desired.
translations.idiomatic: " The Great General had also secretly received the emperor's warning, thinking, "Li Guang is old and his fate is odd—do not let him meet the chanyu, lest he fail to obtain what is desired.

sentences.zh: 」而公孫敖新失侯，大將軍亦欲使敖與俱當單于，故徙前將軍廣。

translations.literal: " Moreover Gongsun Ao had newly lost his marquisate; the Great General also wished to have Ao together meet the chanyu—therefore he moved Forward General Guang.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover Gongsun Ao had newly lost his marquisate; the Great General also wished to have Ao meet the chanyu together—therefore he moved Forward General Guang.

sentences.zh: 廣知之，固自辭於大將軍；

translations.literal: Guang knew this and firmly declined before the Great General;
translations.idiomatic: Guang knew this and firmly declined before the Great General;

sentences.zh: 大將軍不聽，廣不謝而起行，意甚慍怒。

translations.literal: the Great General would not listen; Guang did not thank him and rose to go—his mind very resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: the Great General would not listen; Guang did not thank him and rose to go, deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 大將軍出塞千餘里，度幕，見單于兵陳而待。

translations.literal: The Great General went out beyond the frontier more than a thousand li, crossed the desert screen, and saw the chanyu's troops arrayed and waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The Great General went out more than a thousand li beyond the frontier, crossed the desert, and saw the chanyu's troops arrayed and waiting.

sentences.zh: 於是大將軍令武剛車自環為營，而縱五千騎往當匈奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Great General ordered armored war wagons to ring themselves into a camp, and sent five thousand horsemen forward to meet the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Great General ordered armored war wagons to ring themselves into a camp and sent five thousand horsemen forward to meet the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 匈奴亦縱可萬騎。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu also sent out perhaps ten thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu also sent out perhaps ten thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 會日且入，大風起，砂礫擊面，兩軍不相見，漢益縱左右翼繞單于。

translations.literal: It happened that the sun was about to set, a great wind rose, sand and pebbles struck the face, and the two armies could not see one another; Han further sent the left and right wings to circle around the chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: As the sun was about to set, a great wind rose, sand and pebbles struck the face, and the two armies could not see one another; Han further sent the left and right wings to circle around the chanyu.

sentences.zh: 單于視漢兵多而士馬尚強，自度戰不能如漢兵，單于遂乘六騾，壯騎可數百，直冒漢圍，西北馳去。

translations.literal: The chanyu saw Han troops were many and men and horses still strong; he judged himself unable in battle to match Han troops; the chanyu thereupon mounted six piebald steeds, with picked horsemen numbering perhaps several hundred, dashed straight through the Han encirclement, and fled northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu saw Han troops were many and men and horses still strong; judging he could not match Han in battle, he mounted six piebald steeds with several hundred picked horsemen, dashed straight through the Han encirclement, and fled northwest.

sentences.zh: 時已昏，漢匈奴相紛拏，殺傷大當。

translations.literal: It was already dusk; Han and Xiongnu grappled with one another; killing and wounding were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: It was already dusk; Han and Xiongnu grappled with one another, and killing and wounding were roughly equal.

sentences.zh: 當軍左校捕虜言，單于未昏而去，漢軍發輕騎夜追之，大將軍軍因隨其後，匈奴兵亦散走。

translations.literal: The Left Colonel of the army's captives said the chanyu had left before dusk; Han troops sent light cavalry to pursue by night, and the Great General's army followed after; Xiongnu troops also scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Captives of the army's Left Colonel said the chanyu had left before dusk; Han sent light cavalry to pursue by night, and the Great General's army followed after; Xiongnu troops also scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 遲明，行二百餘里，不得單于，捕斬首虜萬九千級，遂至窴顏山趙信城，得匈奴積粟食軍，留一日，悉燒其城餘粟而歸。

translations.literal: At dawn, having marched more than two hundred li, they did not obtain the chanyu; they captured and beheaded captives numbering nineteen thousand ranks; they then reached Zhijian Mountain and Zhao Xin's city, obtained Xiongnu stored grain to feed the army, stayed one day, and completely burned the city's remaining grain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, having marched more than two hundred li, they did not catch the chanyu; they took nineteen thousand heads and captives; they then reached Zhijian Mountain and Zhao Xin's city, used Xiongnu stored grain to feed the army, stayed one day, burned the city's remaining grain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 前將軍廣與右將軍食其軍無導，惑失道，後大將軍，不及單于戰。

translations.literal: Forward General Guang and Right General Shiyi's army had no guide; confused, they lost the way, lagged behind the Great General, and did not reach the battle with the chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Forward General Guang and Right General Shiyi's army had no guide; confused, they lost the way, fell behind the Great General, and missed the battle with the chanyu.

sentences.zh: 大將軍引還，過幕南，乃遇二將軍。

translations.literal: The Great General led the return, passed south of the desert screen, and thereupon met the two generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Great General led the return, passed south of the desert, and there met the two generals.

sentences.zh: 大將軍使長史責問廣、食其失道狀，急責廣之幕府對簿。

translations.literal: The Great General sent the chief clerk to reproach Guang and Shiyi for losing the way; urgently he summoned Guang to the headquarters for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Great General sent the chief clerk to reproach Guang and Shiyi for losing the way and urgently summoned Guang to headquarters for judgment.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「諸校尉無罪，乃我自失道，吾今自上簿至莫府」。

translations.literal: Guang said: "The various colonels are without guilt—it was your servant himself who lost the way; your servant will now himself go up to account at headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "The colonels are without guilt—it was I myself who lost the way; I will now go myself to account at headquarters."

sentences.zh: 廣謂其麾下曰：「廣結髮與匈奴大小七十餘戰，今幸從大將軍出接單于兵，而大將軍徙廣部行回遠，而又迷失道，豈非天哉！

translations.literal: Guang said to his subordinates: "Guang from tying up hair has with the Xiongnu fought in great and small battles more than seventy times; now fortunately following the Great General out to meet the chanyu's troops, yet the Great General moved Guang's division on a circuitous far route, and moreover we lost the way—is this not Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Guang said to his subordinates, "I have fought the Xiongnu in more than seventy great and small battles since boyhood; now, fortunate to follow the Great General out to meet the chanyu, the Great General moved my division on a circuitous far route, and moreover we lost the way—is this not Heaven!

sentences.zh: 且廣年六十餘矣，終不能復對刀筆之吏！

translations.literal: Moreover Guang is more than sixty years old—I ultimately cannot again face clerks with knife and brush!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I am more than sixty years old—I cannot again face the clerks with knife and brush!

sentences.zh: 」遂引刀自剄。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drew his sword and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he drew his sword and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 廣為人廉，得賞賜輒分其麾下，飲食與士共之，為二千石四十餘年，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Guang as a man was incorrupt; whenever he obtained rewards and gifts he at once divided them among his subordinates; food and drink he shared with the soldiers; as a two-thousand-bushel official for more than forty years, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was incorrupt; whenever he received rewards he at once divided them among his men; he shared food and drink with the soldiers; as a two-thousand-bushel official for more than forty years, his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 猿臂，善射，度不中不發。

translations.literal: Ape arms—skilled at archery; if he judged he would not hit, he did not release.
translations.idiomatic: With arms like an ape's, he was skilled at archery; if he judged he would not hit, he did not release.

sentences.zh: 將兵，乏絕之處見水，士卒不盡飲，廣不近水，士卒不盡食，廣不嘗食。

translations.literal: When leading troops, in places where supplies ran out and they saw water, if the soldiers had not all drunk, Guang did not approach the water; if the soldiers had not all eaten, Guang did not taste food.
translations.idiomatic: When leading troops, in places where supplies ran out, if the soldiers had not all drunk at water, Guang did not approach the water; if they had not all eaten, Guang did not taste food.

sentences.zh: 士以此愛樂為用。

translations.literal: The soldiers for this loved and delighted to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers for this loved him and delighted to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 及死，一軍皆哭。

translations.literal: When he died, the whole army wept.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞之，知與不知，無老壯皆為垂涕。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames heard it; whether they knew him or not, none old or young but shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard it, whether they knew him or not, young and old alike shed tears.

sentences.zh: 而右將軍獨下吏，當死，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: But the Right General alone was sent down to the officials; he should have died but was ransomed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: But the Right General alone was sent to the officials; he should have died but was ransomed and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 單于之遁走，其兵往往與漢兵相亂而隨單于，單于久不與其大眾相得。

translations.literal: As the chanyu fled, his troops often mingled in disorder with Han troops while following the chanyu; the chanyu for a long time did not rejoin his main force.
translations.idiomatic: As the chanyu fled, his troops often mingled in disorder with Han troops while following him; for a long time the chanyu did not rejoin his main force.

sentences.zh: 其右谷蠡王以為單于死，乃自立為單于。

translations.literal: His Right Guli King thought the chanyu was dead and thereupon set himself up as chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: His Right Guli King thought the chanyu was dead and thereupon declared himself chanyu.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，真單于復得其眾，而右谷蠡王乃去其單于號。

translations.literal: After more than ten days the true chanyu regained his followers, and the Right Guli King thereupon cast off his chanyu title.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days the true chanyu regained his followers, and the Right Guli King thereupon abandoned his chanyu title.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍騎兵車重與大將軍軍等，而無裨將，悉以李敢等為大校，當裨將，出代、右北平二千餘里，絕大幕，直左方兵，獲屯頭王、韓王等三人，將軍、相國、當戶、都尉八十三人，封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，登臨翰海，鹵獲七萬四百四十三級。

translations.literal: The Swift Cavalry General's cavalry, chariots, and baggage were equal to the Great General's army, yet he had no lieutenant generals; all used Li Gan and others as grand colonels in place of lieutenant generals; he went out from Dai and Right Beiping more than two thousand li, crossed the great desert screen, struck straight at the left-wing troops, captured Tuntou King, Han King, and three others, eighty-three generals, chancellors, household heads, and commandants; sealed Mount Langjuxu, performed the feng at Guyuan, ascended and looked upon the Han Sea; captive booty numbered seventy thousand four hundred forty-three heads.
translations.idiomatic: Swift Cavalry General Huo Qubing's cavalry, chariots, and baggage matched the Great General's force, yet he had no lieutenant generals; he used Li Gan and others as grand colonels in their place; marching from Dai and Right Beiping more than two thousand li, he crossed the great desert, struck straight at the left-wing troops, captured Tuntou King, Han King, and three others plus eighty-three generals, chancellors, household heads, and commandants; he sealed Mount Langjuxu, performed the feng at Guyuan, and ascended to look upon the Han Sea; captive booty totaled seventy thousand four hundred forty-three heads.

sentences.zh: 天子以五千八百戶益封驃騎將軍；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven increased the Swift Cavalry General's fief by five thousand eight hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor increased Huo Qubing's fief by five thousand eight hundred households;

sentences.zh: 又封其所部右北平太守路博德等四人列侯，從驃侯破奴等二人益封，校尉敢為關內侯，食邑；

translations.literal: moreover he enfeoffed four men of his command including Right Beiping Administrator Lu Bode as full marquises, increased the fiefs of two men including Marquis of Congpiao Ponu, made Colonel Gan a Marquis within the Passes with a food fief;
translations.idiomatic: moreover he enfeoffed four men of his command including Right Beiping Administrator Lu Bode as full marquises, increased the fiefs of two men including Marquis of Congpiao Ponu, and made Colonel Li Gan a Marquis within the Passes with a food fief;

sentences.zh: 軍吏卒為官、賞賜甚多。

translations.literal: army officers and soldiers received offices and rewards in great number.
translations.idiomatic: army officers and soldiers received offices and rewards in great number.

sentences.zh: 而大將軍不得益封，軍吏卒皆無封侯者。

translations.literal: But the Great General received no increase in fief; among army officers and soldiers none were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: But the Great General received no increase in fief, and none of his army officers or soldiers were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 兩軍之出塞，塞閱官及私馬凡十四萬匹，而復入塞者不滿三萬匹。

translations.literal: When the two armies went out beyond the frontier, frontier review officials and private horses totaled one hundred forty thousand head; yet those that re-entered the frontier were fewer than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the two armies went out beyond the frontier, government and private horses totaled one hundred forty thousand; yet fewer than thirty thousand re-entered the frontier.

sentences.zh: 乃益置大司馬位，大將軍、驃騎將軍皆為大司馬，定令，令驃騎將軍秩祿與大將軍等。

translations.literal: Thereupon the post of Grand Marshal was further established; the Great General and Swift Cavalry General were both made Grand Marshals; the order was fixed that the Swift Cavalry General's rank and salary should equal the Great General's.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the post of Grand Marshal was established; the Great General and Swift Cavalry General were both made Grand Marshals, and it was fixed that Huo Qubing's rank and salary should equal Wei Qing's.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，大將軍青日退而驃騎日益貴。

translations.literal: From this onward Great General Qing daily declined while the Swift Cavalry daily grew more honored.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward Wei Qing daily declined while Huo Qubing daily grew more honored.

sentences.zh: 大將軍故人、門下士多去事,驃騎，輒得官爵，唯任安不肯。

translations.literal: The Great General's old acquaintances and retainers mostly went to serve the Swift Cavalry and at once obtained offices and titles; only Ren An would not.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing's old acquaintances and retainers mostly went to serve Huo Qubing and at once obtained offices and titles; only Ren An would not.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍為人，少言不洩，有氣敢往。

translations.literal: The Swift Cavalry General as a man spoke little and did not leak secrets; he had spirit and dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Qubing spoke little and kept secrets; he had spirit and dared advance.

sentences.zh: 天子嘗欲教之孫、吳兵法，對曰：「顧方略何如耳，不至學古兵法。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven once wished to teach him Sun and Wu's art of war; he replied: "Just look at whether the stratagem and method are right—that is all; there is no need to study ancient military texts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wished to teach him Sun and Wu's art of war; he replied, "Just look at whether the stratagem is right—that is all; there is no need to study ancient military texts.

sentences.zh: 」天子為治第，令驃騎視之，對曰：「匈奴未滅，無以家為也！

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven had a residence built for him and ordered the Swift Cavalry General to view it; he replied: "The Xiongnu are not yet destroyed—there is no taking home as one's concern!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had a residence built for him and ordered Huo Qubing to view it; he replied, "The Xiongnu are not yet destroyed—how can I make a home my concern!

sentences.zh: 」由此上益重愛之。

translations.literal: " From this the emperor above increasingly valued and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the emperor valued and loved him all the more.

sentences.zh: 然少貴，不省士，其從軍，天子為遣太官賫數十乘，既還，重車餘棄粱肉，而士有饑者；

translations.literal: Yet from youth he was honored and did not care for soldiers; when he followed the army the Son of Heaven sent the Grand Provisioner with several tens of loads; when he returned, heavy wagons still discarded millet and meat, yet among the soldiers some were hungry;
translations.idiomatic: Yet from youth he was honored and did not care for his men; on campaign the emperor sent the Grand Provisioner with several tens of loads; when he returned, heavy wagons still discarded grain and meat while some of his soldiers went hungry;

sentences.zh: 其在塞外，卒乏糧或不能自振，而驃騎尚穿域蹋鞠，事多此類。

translations.literal: when he was beyond the frontier, soldiers lacked grain or could not rouse themselves, yet the Swift Cavalry General still wore the frontier and kicked the cuju ball—affairs were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: when he was beyond the frontier, soldiers lacked grain or could not support themselves, yet Huo Qubing still played cuju in camp—affairs were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 大將軍為人仁，喜士退讓，以和柔自媚於上。

translations.literal: The Great General as a man was benevolent, delighted in scholars and yielded, using gentleness and softness to please himself before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing was benevolent, delighted in scholars and yielded, and used gentleness to please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 兩人志操如此。

translations.literal: The two men's aims and conduct were thus.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's character was thus.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢所殺虜匈奴合八九萬，而漢士卒物故亦數萬。

translations.literal: At this time those Han killed and captured from the Xiongnu totaled eighty or ninety thousand, while Han soldiers who died also numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han killed and captured eighty or ninety thousand Xiongnu, while Han soldiers who died also numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 是後匈奴遠遁，而幕南無王庭。

translations.literal: After this the Xiongnu fled far away, and south of the desert screen there was no royal court.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Xiongnu fled far away, and south of the desert there was no royal court.

sentences.zh: 漢渡河自朔方以西至令居，往往通渠，置田官，吏卒五六萬人，稍蠶食匈奴以北；

translations.literal: Han crossed the river from west of Shuofang to Lingju, everywhere opening canals, establishing field offices, with fifty or sixty thousand officials and soldiers gradually nibbling north of the Xiongnu;
translations.idiomatic: Han crossed the river from west of Shuofang to Lingju, opened canals everywhere, established field offices, and with fifty or sixty thousand officials and soldiers gradually encroached north of the Xiongnu;

sentences.zh: 然亦以馬少，不復大出擊匈奴矣。

translations.literal: yet also because horses were few, they no longer made great expeditions to strike the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: yet because horses were few, they no longer mounted great expeditions against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 匈奴用趙信計，遣使於漢，好辭請和親。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu used Zhao Xin's plan and sent envoys to Han with pleasing words requesting marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu used Zhao Xin's plan and sent envoys to Han with pleasing words to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 天子下其議，或言和親，或言遂臣之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven circulated the matter for discussion; some spoke of marriage alliance, some of making them subjects at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated the matter for discussion; some spoke of a marriage alliance, some of subjugating them at once.

sentences.zh: 丞相長史任敞曰：「匈奴新破困，宜可使為外臣，朝請於邊。

translations.literal: Chancellor Chief Clerk Ren Chang said: "The Xiongnu are newly defeated and distressed—it is fitting to make them outer subjects who attend court at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chief Clerk Ren Chang said, "The Xiongnu are newly defeated and distressed—it is fitting to make them outer subjects who attend court at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」漢使任敞於單于，單于大怒，留之不遣。

translations.literal: " Han sent Ren Chang to the chanyu; the chanyu was greatly angered and detained him without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: " Han sent Ren Chang to the chanyu; the chanyu was greatly angered and detained him without sending him back.

sentences.zh: 是時，博士狄山議以為和親便，上以問張湯，湯曰：「此愚儒無知。

translations.literal: At this time Academician Di Shan in discussion held that marriage alliance was expedient; the emperor above asked Zhang Tang; Tang said: "These foolish Ru are without knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Academician Di Shan argued that a marriage alliance was expedient; the emperor asked Zhang Tang; Tang said, "These foolish Ru are ignorant.

sentences.zh: 」狄山曰：「臣固愚，愚忠。

translations.literal: " Di Shan said: "Your servant is indeed foolish—foolishly loyal.
translations.idiomatic: " Di Shan said, "Your servant is indeed foolish—foolishly loyal.

sentences.zh: 若御史大夫湯，乃詐忠。

translations.literal: As for Censor-in-Chief Tang, he is falsely loyal.
translations.idiomatic: As for Censor-in-Chief Tang, he is falsely loyal.

sentences.zh: 」於是上作色曰：「吾使生居一郡，能無使虜入盜乎？

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor above changed color and said: "If I place you, sir, in charge of one commandery, can you keep the barbarians from entering to rob?
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor changed color and said, "If I place you in charge of one commandery, can you keep the barbarians from raiding it?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不能。

translations.literal: " He said: "I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I cannot.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「居一縣？

translations.literal: " He said: "In charge of one county?
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "In charge of one county?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不能。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I cannot.

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「居一障間？

translations.literal: " Again he said: "In charge of one beacon interval?
translations.idiomatic: " Again he said, "In charge of one beacon interval?

sentences.zh: 」山自度辯窮且下吏，曰：「能。

translations.literal: " Shan himself judged his argument exhausted and that he would be sent down to the officials, and said: "I can.
translations.idiomatic: " Shan judged his argument exhausted and that he would be sent to the officials, and said, "I can.

sentences.zh: 」於是上遣山乘障，至月餘，匈奴斬山頭而去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor above sent Shan to man the beacon; after more than a month the Xiongnu cut off Shan's head and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor sent Shan to man the beacon; after more than a month the Xiongnu cut off his head and left.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，群臣震懾，無敢忤湯者。

translations.literal: From this onward the ministers were shaken and in awe; none dared oppose Tang.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward the ministers were shaken and in awe; none dared oppose Tang.

sentences.zh: ----5是歲，汲黯坐法免，以定襄太守義縱為右內史，河內太守王溫舒為中尉。

translations.literal: ----5 This year, Ji An was dismissed for violating the law; Dingxiang Administrator Yi Zong was made Right Metropolitan Steward, and Henei Administrator Wang Wenshu was made Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 This year Ji An was dismissed for violating the law; Dingxiang Administrator Yi Zong was made Right Metropolitan Steward, and Henei Administrator Wang Wenshu Commandant of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，寧成為關都尉，吏民出入關者號曰：「寧見乳虎，無值寧成之怒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ning Cheng was Frontier Pass Commandant; officials and people passing in and out of the pass cried: "Better to meet a suckling tiger than to meet Ning Cheng's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ning Cheng was Frontier Pass Commandant; officials and people passing through the pass said, "Better to meet a suckling tiger than to meet Ning Cheng's wrath.

sentences.zh: 」及義縱為南陽太守，至關，寧成側行送迎。

translations.literal: " When Yi Zong became Administrator of Nanyang and reached the pass, Ning Cheng walked sideways to see him off and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi Zong became Administrator of Nanyang and reached the pass, Ning Cheng walked sideways to see him off and welcome him.

sentences.zh: 至郡，遂按寧氏，破碎其家；

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery he thereupon investigated the Ning clan and shattered their household;
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the commandery he investigated the Ning clan and shattered their household;

sentences.zh: 南陽吏民重足一跡。

translations.literal: Nanyang's officials and people stepped as if on overlapping feet with one trace.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang's officials and people stepped as if on overlapping feet with one trace.

sentences.zh: 後徙定襄太守，初至，掩定襄獄中重罪輕系二百餘人，及賓客、昆弟私人視亦二百餘人，一捕，鞠曰「為死罪解脫」。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be Administrator of Dingxiang; when he first arrived he seized more than two hundred in Dingxiang prison who were heavily guilty yet lightly held, and guests, brothers, and private visitors numbering more than two hundred as well; he captured them all at once and tried them, saying "aiding escape from capital crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Administrator of Dingxiang; when he first arrived he seized more than two hundred prisoners in Dingxiang jail who were heavily guilty yet lightly held, plus more than two hundred guests, brothers, and private visitors; he captured them all at once and tried them for "aiding escape from capital crimes."

sentences.zh: 是日，皆報殺四百餘人。

translations.literal: That day all were reported killed—more than four hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: That day more than four hundred were reported executed.

sentences.zh: 其後郡中不寒而慄。
